places.name: Bakery House Creek (ベーカリーハウス クリーク)
places.gf_detail: Creek is a large everyday neighborhood bakery in Saiin that runs a genuine 米粉100％ (100% rice flour) gluten-free line alongside roughly 80 conventional wheat breads. The shop advertises 米粉を100％使用したグルテンフリーのパン and describes its signature 米粉100％グルテンフリー食パン as 卵・乳製品・小麦粉を一切使わず (using absolutely no egg, dairy, or wheat flour). Because the very same premises bakes and slices wheat bread all day, airborne wheat flour and shared equipment mean cross-contact is realistic — this is an OPTIONS venue, not a dedicated celiac-safe one. Celiacs should treat the rice-flour items as allergen-recipe products, not contamination-controlled ones.
places.vegan_detail: The flagship 米粉100％グルテンフリー食パン is explicitly 卵・乳製品・小麦粉不使用 (no egg, dairy, or wheat), so it is incidentally vegan, and some rice-flour cookies may follow. Most of the ~80 breads, however, are standard wheat products with butter/dairy, so vegan choices are limited to a handful of the rice-flour line. Confirm ingredients per item, as recipes vary.
places.hours_raw: 8:00–22:00, open daily (no regular closing day). Note: some listings cite 7:00–20:30 — confirm before visiting.
places.neighborhood: 西院 (Saiin), Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto
places.cuisine: Bakery (rice-flour gluten-free line + wheat breads)
places.notes: [GF] Ask staff directly for the 米粉100％ (100% rice flour) items — the gluten-free 食パン (loaf), rice-flour bagels, cookies and cheesecake. These are made to an egg/dairy/wheat-free recipe, but everything is produced in a shared, high-volume wheat bakery with visible flour dust, so this suits gluten-sensitive/allergy-aware diners rather than highly reactive celiacs. Buy sealed/whole items rather than open-shelf loose bread to reduce cross-contact, and go early as the GF line sells out.

chef_bio.background: Bakery House Creek is a long-running neighborhood bakery on the Saiin shopping street, about three minutes on foot from Hankyu Saiin Station (near Randen Saiin). It is a high-volume everyday shop offering around 80 kinds of bread daily at budget prices (mostly ¥100–200). Japanese coverage notes the shop expanded its rice-flour, gluten-free range over time in response to customer requests, particularly from people with wheat allergies. No individual owner or head-baker name is published in the sources reviewed.
chef_bio.philosophy: An affordable, approachable everyday bakery that has added a dedicated rice-flour gluten-free line so wheat-allergic and health-conscious customers can still buy bread.
chef_bio.specialty: 米粉100％グルテンフリー食パン (100% rice flour gluten-free loaf) and rice-flour bagels, alongside ~80 conventional wheat breads.

anecdotes.text: The gluten-free 米粉食パン is made 卵・乳製品・小麦粉を一切使わず (with no egg, dairy or wheat) to a house recipe, giving a moist, chewy (しっとりもちもち) texture prized by wheat-allergy customers.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 日本語記事（kyotokurasu.jp、kyotogourmet.jp、Tabelog）によれば、西院の商店街にある約80種類のパンを扱う庶民的なベーカリー（阪急西院から徒歩約3分）で、米粉100％のグルテンフリーのパン（卵・乳製品・小麦粉不使用、しっとりもちもち）や米粉ベーグルが名物。オーナー個人名は記載なし。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Full wheat bakery (~80 wheat breads baked and sliced daily on-site) sharing space with the rice-flour line — realistic airborne wheat-flour and shared-equipment cross-contact. OPTIONS tier only.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Vegan-friendly 米粉100％ loaf is baked in the same premises as dairy/butter wheat breads; no separation stated.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No formal allergen-handling protocol published; GF items are recipe-based (卵・乳製品・小麦粉不使用) rather than contamination-controlled. Ask staff which items are 米粉100％.

positives.text: Genuine, clearly labelled 米粉100％ gluten-free line: 米粉100％グルテンフリー食パン made 卵・乳製品・小麦粉を一切使わず, plus rice-flour bagels, cookies and cheesecake.

places.name: coconotane (ここのたね)
places.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. places.name: THE NICOLE / Nicole Naturelle (ザ・ニコル / Nicole Naturelle)
places.gf_detail: THE NICOLE is a conventional Kyoto patisserie that also runs a separate allergen-free sub-line, Nicole Naturelle, whose sweets are made with 100% domestic rice flour and no wheat. The venue's own site states 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』 and describes the line as 『卵、乳、白砂糖不使用』『グルテンフリー』『ヴィーガンスイーツ』 using 国産米粉100%. However, the SAME shop bakes ordinary wheat flour cakes and serves 欧風スパイスカレー (European-style spice curry, typically a wheat-roux base), so the kitchen is shared and cross-contact with wheat flour is a real risk — celiacs must confirm the item is from the Naturelle line and ideally order it pre-made/sealed. Because of the shared wheat kitchen this stays an 'options' venue, not a dedicated GF facility.
places.vegan_detail: The Nicole Naturelle line is fully plant-based — 卵・乳・動物性油脂不使用, using 京豆腐 (Kyoto tofu), 豆乳ヨーグルト (soy yogurt), soy-based 'butter', coconut oil and maple syrup in place of dairy and eggs. These items are explicitly marketed as ヴィーガンスイーツ. The parent THE NICOLE shop, though, also sells conventional cakes with egg/dairy and non-vegan curry, so only the Naturelle line is vegan — choose from it specifically.
places.hours_raw: 10:30-16:00; closed Mondays and Tuesdays (per the venue's own site). Nicole Naturelle allergen-free sweets are by reservation / online order only. Hours differ between sources (Tabelog lists Mon-Fri 10:30-18:00, Sat 10:30-17:00, closed Sun) - confirm before visiting.

Order Naturelle items specifically (they are reservation/online-order only, sold mostly as whole tarts, chocolate and sablé tins) and confirm the item is from the allergen line. Cash only; small counter shop in the Horikawa shopping arcade.

chef_bio.background: Owner-pâtissier 堀口微笑琉 was born in 1979 in Kyoto's Nishijin district and trained at several patisseries between 1999 and 2006 before opening his own shop, 洋菓子屋Sorcier, in Umeda in 2008. The business relocated and evolved over the years — becoming Kitchen&Cake NICOLE in 2015 and rebranding as THE NICOLE at the current 西陣 (Nishijin) location in 2019. In 2022 he added a spice-curry operation (麺屋 微笑琉 / NICOLEカレー, a once-a-week spice-curry-udon venture), and in 2023 he launched the Nicole Naturelle allergen-free, vegan, gluten-free sweets line. The shop's stated aim is 「食材の制限がある方も楽しめるスイーツ」— sweets that people with dietary restrictions can also enjoy.
chef_bio.philosophy: A hybrid patisserie-and-curry café built around inclusivity and low-sugar / low-fat, 'body-friendly' sweets, with the Nicole Naturelle line created so that people with egg, dairy and wheat restrictions can still enjoy cakes.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour (米粉) vegan gluten-free tarts, 京豆腐 tofu-based raw-chocolate confections and 黒糖 sablé tins; also European-style spice curry.

anecdotes.text: The venture is a 洋菓子×スパイスカレー hybrid — a Western-confectionery shop that also serves a meat-free 'Nicole curry' deriving umami from vegetables, plus rotating daily creative spice curries.
The allergen-free Nicole Naturelle line was launched in 2023, years after the base patisserie, specifically to serve customers with dietary restrictions.

places.name: OUBON (オーボン)
places.gf_detail: OUBON is a conventional Western pâtisserie near Fushimi Inari that sells regular wheat cakes AND a separate allergy-oriented 米粉 (rice-flour) line, so wheat is handled in the same kitchen. The shop's own claim for the rice-flour line reads: 「全てに米粉を使用していますのでアレルギーをお持ちの方でも、もちろん食べていただけます」 ("Everything uses rice flour, so even those with allergies can of course eat it"). Because the same bakery also produces wheat pastries daily, cross-contact with gluten is a real risk and this cannot be treated as celiac-safe — confirm with staff and buy only the labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー items.
places.vegan_detail: The rice-flour items are not vegan: the shop lists 卵 (egg) and 乳 (dairy) as allergens on its gluten-free products. The signature 豆乳米粉ロール is described as 「グルテンフリー商品となっており、アレルギー物質は卵、乳」 and uses Hokkaido cream (whipped with soymilk), so egg and dairy remain. No vegan line is advertised.
places.hours_raw: 10:00–20:00, closed Wednesdays (some listings show Wed 12:00–18:00). Tel 075-632-8287.
places.neighborhood: 京都市伏見区深草鈴塚町 (Fukakusa, Fushimi-ku — near Fushimi Inari)
places.cuisine: Western pâtisserie / cakes & baked sweets (rice-flour GF line)
places.notes: [GF] Not celiac-safe — this is a shared wheat kitchen. OUBON bakes conventional wheat cakes alongside its 米粉 (rice-flour) allergy line, so gluten cross-contact is likely; only the explicitly labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー sweets (e.g. 豆乳米粉ロール, 米粉フィナンシェ, 米粉マドレーヌ) are wheat-free by recipe, and even those are baked in the same premises. Also note the GF items contain egg and dairy. Tabelog currently lists the shop's operating status as unconfirmed/on-hold, so phone ahead (075-632-8287) to confirm it is open before visiting.

roles: Head pastry chef (シェフパティシエ)
chef_bio.background: OUBON opened in December 2017 a few minutes' walk from Fushimi Inari station in Fukakusa, Fushimi-ku. Head pastry chef and owner Nobuo Kakine (垣根信夫) is described as a veteran patissier with 40 years of experience in Kyoto, having served as head pâtissier at a well-known hotel and other shops before opening his own. The shop is credited as being run by a pâtissier who helped pioneer Japanese-style (和風) sweets. For its gluten-free line OUBON sources rice flour from Asahi Seifunjo (朝日製粉所) in the Kyoto Tamba/Nantan area.
chef_bio.philosophy: To make rice-flour cakes so close to wheat versions that they are hard to tell apart in a blind test, so that people with wheat allergies can enjoy ordinary-tasting Western sweets alongside everyone else.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour (米粉) gluten-free cakes and baked sweets — signature 豆乳米粉ロール, plus financiers and madeleines — alongside a conventional wheat pâtisserie range.

anecdotes.text: The shop says its rice-flour sponge is so like wheat that even a blind taste test can't reveal the difference: 「小麦を使っているケーキと食感は全く同じで、味もブラインドテストをしてもわからないほど」.
OUBON's gluten-free cakes are made with rice flour supplied by Asahi Seifunjo, a Kyoto Tamba (Nantan) flour mill that profiled the shop and its 40-year-veteran chef.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: オーボンは2017年12月に伏見稲荷近くにオープンした洋菓子店。シェフパティシエの垣根信夫氏は京都で40年の実績を持つベテランで、有名ホテルのチーフパティシエを歴任。通常の小麦のケーキに加え、朝日製粉所の米粉を使ったアレルギー対応・グルテンフリーのケーキを製造。元祖和風スイーツを編み出したパティシエとして紹介されている。

gf_cross_contamination.text: OUBON is a conventional pâtisserie that handles both wheat cakes and rice-flour cakes: 「通常の小麦を使ったケーキや洋菓子、グルテンフリーなケーキやスイーツなどを扱っているお店」. Shared wheat kitchen means airborne-flour and shared-equipment cross-contact risk; not celiac-safe.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not applicable — this is a dessert/patisserie shop; no savory soy-sauce dishes on offer.

vegan_cross_contact.text: GF items are not vegan by recipe — egg (卵) and dairy (乳) are listed as allergens on the rice-flour products, so vegan cross-contact is moot.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop markets the rice-flour line as 「アレルギー対応の米粉ケーキ」 (allergy-conscious rice-flour cakes) and states allergens for the roll as egg and dairy, indicating some allergen awareness, but no dedicated-line or celiac protocol is claimed.

positives.text: A named, clearly-labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー range (roll, financiers, madeleines, shortcake, lemon cake) with rice flour sourced from Asahi Seifunjo, made by a 40-year-veteran chef — a convenient wheat-free sweet stop right by Fushimi Inari.

places.name: 土佐屋 室戸 (Tosaya Muroto)
places.gf_detail: A Tosa (Kōchi) izakaya built on charcoal yakitori and seared bonito (katsuo tataki) — soy sauce, yakitori tare and ponzu (all typically wheat-based) run through the menu, so it is not celiac-safe by default. Some items can be gluten-free if confirmed: sashimi, salt (shio) skewers, and salt-style katsuo tataki without ponzu. But the shared charcoal grill, shared fryer and wheat-containing sauces make cross-contamination likely — order shio, skip the tare/ponzu, and show the celiac card.
places.vegan_detail: A Tosa seafood-and-yakitori counter: seared bonito, charcoal chicken, and shamo (game-fowl) hot pot. Bonito dashi and fish run through almost everything, so even vegetable dishes likely carry animal-derived stock. A few plain vegetable skewers or pickles may be possible, but confirm dashi/bonito with the chef. Not a vegan destination.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00. Closed Sunday. (Some listings also note the 2nd & 3rd Monday closed and lunch by reservation only — confirm before visiting.)
places.neighborhood: Kiyamachi · Kawaramachi-Sanjo (Nakagyo)
places.cuisine: Tosa (Kōchi) izakaya · yakitori & katsuo tataki
places.notes: [Mom & Pop — a Tosa master, ~50 years at the counter] A tiny Kōchi (Tosa) izakaya on Kiyamachi just south of Sanjo — up on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant, with a ~10-seat counter plus one small tatami (6–8). The chef, a Tosa native with roughly half a century behind the grill, cooks yakitori over Tosa binchōtan charcoal and serves Kōchi's signature seared bonito (katsuo tataki), shamo (game-fowl) hot pot, and seasonal Tosa dishes. Reviewers praise thick, odorless bonito and carefully grilled skewers, and a charming old-Kyoto exterior; it draws locals and food-loving visitors alike. Reservations accepted (HotPepper). Address: 河原町通三条下ル大黒町49 (entrance on Kiyamachi-dōri). Instagram @tosayamuroto.

chef_bio.origin: Tosa (Kōchi Prefecture); the shop is in Kiyamachi, Nakagyo Ward, Kyoto
chef_bio.background: A Tosa (Kōchi) native who by most accounts has spent roughly fifty years cooking, running a small counter izakaya devoted to the food of his home region. He grills over Tosa binchōtan (the prized white charcoal of Kōchi) and centers the menu on Kōchi's most famous dish, seared bonito — the kind of veteran, single-counter kitchen where the chef works in front of you and the seasons drive what's served.
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal yakitori over Tosa binchōtan and Kōchi's signature katsuo (bonito) tataki, plus shamo (game-fowl) hot pot and seasonal Tosa dishes.

anecdotes.text: Regulars single out the bonito tataki as thick, generous and completely free of any fishy odor — the hallmark of well-handled katsuo — and note that each yakitori skewer is grilled with real care over binchōtan.

The shop is described as an izakaya serving 'the finest yakitori in Kyoto' by a chef with about 50 years of experience, originally from Tosa in Kōchi Prefecture, with a charming, old-Kyoto exterior that draws both locals and foreign guests.
It sits on Kiyamachi just south of Sanjo, upstairs on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant — an easy-to-miss counter that rewards those who seek it out.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Japanese listings (Tabelog 郷土料理/焼き鳥, Retty, hitosara, navikyo, HotPepper) describe 土佐屋室戸 as a small Kōchi (Tosa) izakaya at 河原町通三条下ル大黒町49, entrance on Kiyamachi, on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant, with a ~10-seat counter and one small tatami room (6–8). Open Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00, closed Sunday; phone 075-221-3056; reservations accepted. The taishō, a Tosa native, is credited with ~50 years of experience; signatures are binchōtan yakitori, katsuo (bonito) tataki, and shamo hot pot, with seasonal Kōchi fare.

cultural_comfort.note: A small veteran-run counter on Kiyamachi that does see foreign diners and takes online reservations — but it's a Japanese izakaya led by a ~50-year chef, with little to no English. A reservation, a few words of Japanese, and easy counter manners go a long way.

gf_cross_contamination.text: This is a yakitori-and-izakaya counter, not a celiac-safe kitchen. Skewers are grilled over a shared charcoal grill alongside tare-basted (wheat soy sauce) items, and any battered/fried dishes share oil, so cross-contamination with wheat is likely across the menu.

Naturally gluten-free choices may exist if confirmed — sashimi, salt (shio) skewers, and salt-style katsuo tataki without ponzu — but they must be ordered explicitly shio/no-sauce and confirmed with the chef.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Yakitori tare, ponzu for the katsuo tataki, and nabe broths are built on Japanese soy sauce, which typically contains wheat. Assume these sauces contain gluten unless the chef confirms a wheat-free alternative; ordering shio (salt) avoids the tare.

vegan_cross_contact.text: A fish- and meat-forward Tosa izakaya (bonito, chicken, game-fowl hot pot) with bonito dashi throughout — even vegetable dishes likely carry animal-derived stock. There is no documented vegan menu; confirm each item with the chef.

positives.text: A tiny, owner-run counter where the chef cooks directly in front of you, so you can ask about ingredients and preparation face-to-face — easiest with some Japanese or a translation app.

places.name: らーめん ふくちあん 二条城前店 (Ramen Fukuchian Nijōjō-mae)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The chain's own allergen chart lists wheat (小麦) in every ramen, set, side and topping on it — including the chashu, seasoned egg and menma — and the noodles are made in-house from wheat flour. The shop says it cooks with ordinary shared utensils and dishes and leaves cross-contamination to the diner's own judgment. The only food item the chart shows without wheat is the sherbet. Not suitable for celiacs.
places.vegan_detail: The regular bowls are built on a pork-bone and chicken-frame soup and topped with pork; the allergen chart lists pork and chicken for all of them. The shop does advertise a 'vegetarian ramen' (miso-based broth, house-made noodles), but in its own words it is made with 'almost no' (ほぼ) meat or fish ingredients — so do not assume it is vegan. Ask what the remaining animal ingredients are before ordering.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:00 (last order 20:30). Closed over the New Year.
places.neighborhood: Oshibori-chō, Nakagyō-ku (NE corner of Horikawa-Oike, opposite Nijō Castle; 3 min from Nijōjō-mae Stn)
places.cuisine: Tonkotsu-shoyu ramen (Fukuchiyama chain) · kara-age · gyoza
places.notes: [Ramen · Fukuchiyama chain] The Kyoto-city branch of ふくちあん, a ramen company from Fukuchiyama in northern Kyoto Prefecture, on the northeast corner of the Horikawa-Oike crossing, across the road from Nijō Castle; it opened in 2022. The house bowl is a pork-bone and Tamba chicken-frame soup simmered for 20+ hours, seasoned with a brewed soy tare aged a year in cedar barrels, over thin house-made noodles, and comes with two kinds of pork, a seasoned egg and green onion. Kara-age is the other draw — the shop advertises a Karaage Grand Prix gold award. You buy a ticket at the machine; an English menu is posted outside and many of the customers are overseas visitors. The shop also advertises a miso-based vegetarian ramen.

roles: ramen company (株式会社新福知庵), Fukuchiyama
chef_bio.origin: Fukuchiyama, northern Kyoto Prefecture — the chain's main shop is by JR Fukuchiyama Station
chef_bio.background: Fukuchian began as a change of trade: in 1996 a Fukuchiyama textile firm turned itself into a ramen business and opened the first ふくちあん. The company has since added branches in Kaibara, Kitaōji (Kyoto), Nijō-jō-mae (2022) and Shiga.
chef_bio.philosophy: The founding-spirit essay on the company site: no textbook, soup after soup poured away, and the temptation to make life easier with ready-made soy tare and stock — refused, because "I don't want to tell a lie" (ウソは嫌なんです).
chef_bio.specialty: Ramen in a pork-bone and Tamba chicken soup with a year-aged brewed soy tare and house-made thin noodles; tender kara-age.

anecdotes.text: Fukuchian started in 1996, when 丸三加工, a Fukuchiyama textile company hit by the industry moving overseas, renamed itself 株式会社福知庵 and became a ramen shop. The Nijō-jō-mae branch opened in 2022.

The soup: Japanese pork leg bones are washed, blanched to remove blood and scum, then simmered in a large pot with Tamba chicken frames, negi and plenty of onion — more than 20 hours in all. It is finished with a brewed soy sauce aged a full year in cedar barrels.
The noodles are made in-house from Nisshin's 特ナンバーワン flour with Inner-Mongolian kansui and 天外天 salt, kneaded, layered, rolled and rested before cutting.
The shop advertises a gold award at the Karaage Grand Prix (からあげグランプリ金賞受賞) for its kara-age.

A June 2026 diner noted the English menu posted outside and the overseas customers inside, ordered the 特濃 (extra-rich) Fukuchian ramen, and praised its slightly sweet pork-bone broth with crunchy bean sprouts and thick chashu.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト(fukuchian.jp)より、株式会社新福知庵(福知山市)。平成8年に繊維業の丸三加工が株式会社福知庵に商号変更しラーメン専門店へ業態変更、ふくちあん本店開店。令和4年 二条城前店開店。二条城前店: 京都市中京区東堀川通御池上る押堀町45-1、TEL 075-212-7620、11:00〜21:00(L.O.20:30)、年中無休(年始を除く)、27席。スープは国産げん骨と丹波産鶏ガラを20時間以上炊く豚骨、元ダレは杉樽で一年熟成の本醸造醤油、自家製麺は日清「特ナンバーワン」。アレルギー表では全ラーメン・サイド・トッピングに小麦。Instagram(2026/10/03)でベジタリアンラーメン(味噌ベース、自家製麺、肉・魚の成分を「ほぼ」使用せず)を告知。

cultural_comfort.note: Order and pay at the ticket machine (electronic money and QR payments accepted, no credit cards). An English menu is posted outside and the shop sees many overseas visitors on their way to or from Nijō Castle; expect a queue on weekends.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The chain's allergen chart lists 小麦 (wheat) for every ramen, set, side dish and topping on it, and the shop states it cooks with ordinary kitchen utensils and ordinarily washed dishes, asking diners to judge cross-contamination risk for themselves.
The noodles are made in-house from wheat flour (Nisshin 特ナンバーワン).

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The base tare (元ダレ) is a brewed soy sauce (本醸造醤油), combined with the pork-bone soup for every shoyu-style bowl.
On the allergen chart even the toppings — トロチャーシュー, バラチャーシュー, 味玉 and メンマ — list 小麦, so a "no noodles" order does not get you to a wheat-free bowl.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The soup is pork leg bone and Tamba chicken frames simmered together for 20+ hours.
The vegetarian ramen has a miso-based broth and is made with 'almost no' (ほぼ) meat or fish ingredients, in the shop's own words — not stated to be vegan.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The chain publishes a per-dish allergen chart (Japanese) that counts allergens shared during processing or cooking as "contained", not only those in the recipe.

places.name: shiro (しろ)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. There is one chef's-choice course, and Tabelog says the shop does not change it for disliked ingredients; nothing is said about allergies. 2026 courses included pasta (cold Siciliana, maltagliati, chestnut pasta), a baguette with olive oil, a fried anago dish and a financier made with rice flour.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: one fixed course built on fish, prosciutto, duck, lamb and beef (2026 reviews), which the shop does not change for dislikes (Tabelog).
places.hours_raw: Wed–Fri dinner 18:00–21:00; Sat–Sun lunch 12:00–14:30 and dinner 18:00–21:00; closed Monday and Tuesday (Tabelog). Every sitting starts at once: lunch at 12:00 (doors 11:45), dinner at 18:00 (doors 17:45) (official site); late arrivals may miss dishes, and the course runs about two hours (Tabelog; an October 2026 diner stayed about two and a half). Reservation only, online (Tabelog). Guests 13 and over only; no strong perfume or very casual clothes (Tabelog). 8 counter seats; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). One drink per person is required (October 2026 review). Opened 14 August 2024 (Tabelog; Leaf Kyoto).
places.neighborhood: 室町通二条下ル, IDO KYOTO 2F (a black-walled building with a courtyard, set back from the street) — 3 min from Karasuma Oike Stn
places.cuisine: One chef's-choice course of about 13 dishes, the same at lunch and dinner, changing gradually over two months: Italian at the base, with Japanese and French technique, built on ingredients from the chef's home prefecture of Shimane and Kyoto vegetables, cooked with well water drawn in the building (Tabelog; official site) · omakase course ¥21,000; with about seven wines ¥32,000; with about seven teas ¥29,000; plus 10% service (Tabelog, tax included); the official site lists lunch and dinner at ¥19,800 including tax and service · signature: fried anago wrapped in freshly shaved prosciutto (2026 reviews) · examples: a cold soup of charred Manganji pepper and cucumber, Yato River ayu cooked seven hours with uruka and a funazushi sauce, 18-month black-pork prosciutto with peach and goat-cheese mousse, Shimane glutinous-rice risotto with shibazuke, cold Siciliana pasta with shrimp and bottarga, maltagliati with lamb and pecorino, Nanatani duck, a rice-flour financier (August 2026); squid and tomato risotto (June 2026); kumquat and burrata (May 2026); persimmon with prosciutto, Tanba chestnut pasta with truffle (October 2026); rice with nodoguro, dried tomato and bitter melon (September 2026) · wine pairings by a sommelier, tea pairings, house sodas such as plum or ume-cardamom
places.notes: [Italian · Karasuma Oike, a Shimane chef's 8-seat counter] Set back from Muromachi-dori, on the second floor of the black-walled IDO KYOTO building with its courtyard, eight seats wrap an open island kitchen in a white room of natural wood. Chef Atsushi Takenaka, from Hamada in Shimane, ran the restaurant Mia Paese there before moving to Kyoto in 2024 to aim higher. The single course, served to everyone at once, starts from Italian cooking and borrows from Japanese and French: Shimane seafood, ayu and rice, Kyoto vegetables and well water from the building's garden. The fried anago wrapped in prosciutto comes from the old restaurant. Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze and Italian WEST 100 (2025); the Michelin Guide's site lists it with a star. Diners in 2026 praise the wine and tea pairings and a friendly chef who explains each dish; some return every season. Guests 13 and over; closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

roles: Owner-chef (Leaf Kyoto: "says the owner, Mr. Takenaka"; official site)
chef_bio.origin: Born and raised in Hamada, Shimane Prefecture (Leaf Kyoto).
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: entered the culinary world at 24; opened ミアパエーゼ (Mia Paese) in Shimane at 30; selected by Gault&Millau in 2020; supervised food as a "food artisan" for JR West's Twilight Express 瑞風; moved to Kyoto in 2024 and opened shiro. Leaf Kyoto (October 2024) adds that the chef grew interested in cooking while working part-time at a restaurant as a university student, worked in an office after graduating, trained at an Italian restaurant, and closed Mia Paese in Hamada in May 2024 to "aim for a higher rank"; the staff all hail from Hamada. A September 2026 diner calls the chef young and notes seven years of running a restaurant deep in the Shimane mountains; another (April 2026) notes partnerships with Shimane farmers, farms and roasters. Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025. The Michelin Guide's page shows a star (read November 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Shiro" (white) is not just a colour but blank space and purity, "nothing there, yet a sense that something is coming"; five rules: keep harmony, respect nature, make space, stay simple, lead to emotion (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Fried anago with prosciutto; Shimane ingredients in Italian form.

anecdotes.text: "The chef, originally from Shimane, has partnered with local farmers, farms, and roasteries to incorporate an abundance of Shimane ingredients into the menu." — April 2026.
"I didn't have any alcohol, but since there was a one-drink order policy per person, I opted for a homemade ume and cardamom soda." — October 2026.
"This was my fourth visit, and each time the experience gets better." — October 2026, caramelised figs and foie gras with a smoky wine.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ido-kyoto.com/shiro): 白 (しろ)、IDO KYOTO 2F (1F は IDOCHA と KOKE)、庭の井戸から汲んだ湧き水を使う、コンセプト「しろ」は単なる色ではない、余白、潔白、しろ五則 (調和を保つこと、自然を尊むこと、余白を生むこと、簡素であること、感動を導くこと)、竹中厚志: 24歳で料理の世界に入る、30歳で島根でミアパエーゼOPEN、2020年 Gault&Millau に選出、JR西日本 Twilight Express 瑞風で食の匠として料理監修、2024年に京都へ移転し「しろ」として開店、ランチ12:00スタート (開場11:45)、ディナー18:00スタート (開場17:45)、19,800円 (税・サービス料込)、水・木・金はディナー、土・日はランチとディナー、月・火休み。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2025、おまかせコース21,000円、ワインペアリング付き32,000円、お茶のペアリング付き29,000円、サービス料10%、カウンター8席、13歳以上、2024年8月14日オープン。口コミ(2026年3月〜10月): 穴子のフリットとプロシュート、Shimane と京都の食材、ペアリング、一斉スタート、1人1ドリンク。

cultural_comfort.note: One set course booked online; the chef explains each dish at the counter (2026).

places.name: 御幸町 田がわ (Goko Machi Tagawa)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; the official site asks guests to check dishes and ingredients with the shop. A Japanese course seasoned with soy sauce and miso; 2026 courses included a dried persimmon fried in Domyoji coating, fried sesame tofu with red miso (October) and soba with salmon roe (September).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Japanese omakase course built on dashi, fish, wagyu and duck (2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Daily from 18:00, one sitting (Tabelog lists 18:00–22:00; official site 18:00–20:30 last entry); closed irregularly (Tabelog; official site); other times can be discussed, and private lunches are taken for groups of five or more (Tabelog). Reservation only, online or by phone between about 11:00 and 17:00 (official site); same-day cancellations are charged 100% (official site; Tabelog). Seats: 10 at the counter (Tabelog) or 12 (official site), a sunken kotatsu-style counter where shoes come off, so wear socks (Tabelog). No strong perfume; bring a light jacket, as the air conditioning varies by seat (Tabelog). Children: ask by phone first (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog; official site). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners; Discover per the official site); no e-money or QR (Tabelog); service charge 10% (Tabelog). Opened 7 February 2017 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Omakase Japanese course of about 10 dishes, changing monthly, cooked in front of the counter with seasonal grilling over Kishu binchotan in ceramic hearths (official site; Tabelog) · omakase course ¥29,040 (Tabelog, tax included) or ¥26,400 (official course page; prices vary with the day's buying); New Year course (1–5 January) ¥33,000; flower-pepper hot-pot course in April ¥33,000; matsuba-crab course for whole-shop groups of eight or more and crab nights (December–February), from about ¥44,000; plus 10% service (official site; Tabelog) · seafood from ama divers in the chef's home prefecture of Mie, A5 black wagyu (Tabelog) · several clay-pot rices to finish, such as ginkgo rice, eel rice and white rice with the meat's mushroom sauce (September 2026) · autumn Matsutake course at private events (¥40,000–59,999 per diner, October 2026): Iwate Matsutake rice, grilled Matsutake, Akashi sea bream, Kesennuma bonito tataki, a hassun of ayu with roe, Kagoshima black wagyu and more, then nodoguro and chicken-and-burdock clay-pot rice · September 2026: corn tofu with sea urchin, Matsutake and eel in kuzu sauce, Fukui eel grilled in front of the diner, Hyogo black wagyu shabu-shabu in a mushroom sauce · sake such as Eiketsu, Jikon, Tokujirou (September 2026)
places.notes: [Kappo · south of the Kyoto Gyoen, a former engineer's charcoal-hearth counter] A renovated machiya south of the Kyoto Gyoen, behind lattice, earthen walls and a yellow hemp noren, with a hinoki counter where guests sit with their feet in a sunken well and watch everything cooked over binchotan in ceramic hearths. Owner Yoshiaki Tagawa, born in Mie in 1976, left engineering for the kitchen at 25 and opened here in 2017 after training at well-known Japanese restaurants, with the theme of fine Japanese food enjoyed without stiffness. One course a month of about ten dishes: seafood from Mie ama divers, A5 wagyu, and two or three clay-pot rices at the end (one regular keeps lunch light on Tagawa days). Spring brings a flower-pepper hot pot, autumn a Matsutake feast. Tabelog Award Bronze every year from 2018 to 2026; the shop's site says it holds a Michelin star. Diners in 2026 describe a lively, laughing counter and an owner one compared to the actor Masato Sakai.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshiaki Tagawa (Tabelog's chef section; an October 2026 review gives "Yoshitaka Tagawa")
roles: Owner and chef (Tabelog: "the welcoming owner"; official site: 店主)
chef_bio.origin: Mie Prefecture, born 1976 (Tabelog); Matsusaka City in Mie, per an October 2026 review.
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in Mie Prefecture in 1976; changed from engineer to chef at 25, drawn by the "one-on-one interactions" between chefs and customers over a counter; trained at Masago Saryo (Yokohama), Gion Maruyama (Kyoto) and Kumura (Azabu-Juban); opened Tagawa in Gokomachi in February 2017. An October 2026 review lists Gion Maruyama and Azabu Yukimura. A March 2024 diner writes that the owner entered the trade "at a much older age than typical chefs, training under younger seniors at a renowned restaurant". The official site says the owner buys the fish, meat and Kyoto vegetables daily and the flowers for the room as well, and that the restaurant has a Michelin star. The ceramic hearth was passed down from the owner's master (Tabelog). Staff: apprentices (October 2026) and a Ms. Tanaka, thanked for warm hospitality in an October 2026 review. Tabelog Award Bronze 2018–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025. The site's news notes a collaboration event in Miami in May 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Casually enjoying exquisite Japanese dishes" (気軽に味わう和の逸品): hospitality that keeps guests from feeling formal, and conversation across a flat counter (official site; Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal grilling in ceramic hearths; clay-pot rices; spring flower-pepper hot pot; autumn Matsutake.

anecdotes.text: "The private reservation event was lively, with the owner resembling Masato Sakai, who is currently starring in a popular drama." — October 2026, Matsutake course.
"On flower pepper days, there are four types of rice dishes, including zosui (rice porridge)." — April 2026, a regular's fourteenth visit.
"This year's fish lacks fat, so instead of slow-roasting it, [the chef] quickly grilled it using both top and bottom charcoal heat." — September 2026, Pacific saury.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gokoumachi-tagawa.com): 御幸町 田がわ、夷川通御幸町西入松本町575、テーマは「気軽に味わう和の逸品」、硬くならないおもてなし、フラットなカウンター越しに目の前で調理、陶器で作られた炉と備長炭、ミシュランひとつ星を獲得、店主出身地の三重県をはじめ様々な産地の旬の素材、おまかせコースのみで一品料理なし、コースは10品前後で毎月変更、おまかせコース26,400円 (別ページに21,780円の記載も)、お正月特別料理33,000円、花山椒鍋特別コース33,000円 (4月)、松葉蟹の特別コース・蟹の会は参考価格44,000円、仕入れで価格が変動、料理内容・食材は店舗に確認を、完全予約制、電話は11:00〜17:00ごろ、営業時間18:00〜20:30 (最終入店)、不定休、カウンター12席、全席禁煙、当日キャンセル100%、店主が花も仕入れる。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2018〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、おまかせコース29,040円、サービス料10%、カウンター10席、足を下ろせるカウンターで靴を脱ぐ、靴下着用、2017年2月7日オープン。口コミ(2026年1月〜10月): Matsutake の会、花山椒の鍋、土鍋ご飯が数種類、Mie の ama の魚介、店主は Masato Sakai に似ているという声、Tanaka さんのもてなし。

places.cuisine: One omakase course, "Idee e Sapori" (ideas and creations of chef Nemoto), the same at lunch and dinner, changing monthly: amuse, prosciutto, panzerotti, salad, pasta or risotto, fish, meat, palate cleanser, pasta, dessert, petits fours (official site) · course ¥19,800; half pairing (5 glasses) +¥6,600; full pairing (8 or more) +¥9,900; plus 10% service (official site, tax included; Tabelog lists the totals ¥26,400 and ¥29,700; prices rose in January 2026) · wines from a walk-in cellar of about 600 bottles, plus sake, beer, whisky, teas and non-alcoholic wines (official site) · handmade pasta and seafood in the style of Emilia-Romagna, where the chef trained (Tabelog) · October 2026: celery-root chips with gelato and caviar; hairy crab with early mikan; prosciutto with fried gnocco; a foie-gras cream puff; panzerotti of fresh porcini and lobster; a tart of 11 autumn vegetables; raviolone of egg yolk, chicken, chestnut and sansho oil; maitake fritters and barracuda risotto; aged beef fillet with turnip; a Muscat Collins palate cleanser; Pacific saury and fennel chitarra; tiramisu · September 2026: a 10-vegetable "pinzimonio" of jelly, sorbet and mousse; pistachio and lobster capellini that the chef said was inspired by dan dan noodles; grouper risotto; porcini tagliatelle · takeaway roast beef and New Year osechi (official site)
places.notes: [Italian · Marutamachi, a former kaiseki cook's Italian omakase] A renovated Kyoto townhouse near Marutamachi station with an eight-seat counter facing a display of the day's vegetables. Owner-chef Yoshihiko Nemoto, born in Shiga in 1977, cooked Japanese food for about ten years (ぎをん浜作 in Kyoto, then Kitashinchi in Osaka) before going to Italy at 29 and training at Ristorante Magnolia; the shop opened in 2013 and took its present form in 2021. One course for everyone at once, about a dozen plates with two pasta courses, light and playful rather than heavy: an 11-vegetable tart, panzerotti of porcini and lobster, a dan-dan-inspired pistachio capellini. Pairings come from a walk-in cellar of some 600 bottles. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019, 2025 and 2026, Italian WEST 100 (2021, 2023, 2025), and a Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026 Selected restaurant. Book online only; closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, and for an autumn break until 5 November 2026.

chef_bio.specialty: Handmade pasta; panzerotti; vegetable tarts and salads.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (radice-kyoto.com): RADICE〈ラディーチェ〉、鏡屋町50番地、丸太町駅6番出口から徒歩3分、ランチ (金土日祝のみ) 12:00一斉スタート、ディナー (木〜月曜日) 18:30一斉スタート、定休日は火曜・水曜、予約はオンラインのみ、2026年10月27日〜11月5日は秋季休暇、シェフ根本嘉彦: 1977年滋賀県生まれ、15歳から料理人の道へ、京都の「ぎをん浜作」と大阪の北新地で約10年和食、29歳でイタリアへ、Ristorante Magnolia で約2年修行、祇園t.v.b と Vineria t.v.b でシェフ、2013年にオーナーシェフとして RistoriaRadice をオープン、2021年にリニューアルして現在の Radice に。おまかせコース1種類 “Idee e Sapori” 19,800円 (税込、別途サービス料10%)、ランチ・ディナー共通、ペアリングはフル (8種類〜) 9,900円、ハーフ (5種類) 6,600円、約600本のウォークインのワインセラー、ミシュランガイド京都・大阪2026でセレクテッドレストラン、ローストビーフのテイクアウト、御節。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019・2025・2026、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、12席 (カウンター8、テーブル1卓4名)、10歳未満不可、ベランダに喫煙スペース、2013年12月21日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 11種類の野菜のタルト、パンツェロッティ、ピスタチオとオマールのカッペリーニ、パスタの会、町家を改装した店内。

places.cuisine: Modern French with Chinese technique and Kyoto ingredients, from a chef who cooked Chinese food for about ten years (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · lunch "Collection de Saison" about 10 dishes ¥13,200; lunch "Gourmand" (lobster starter, beef main) ¥18,700; dinner "Création" about 13 dishes ¥25,300 (Tabelog: 12; also served at lunch); special room lunch ¥27,500, dinner ¥46,200; plus 10% service (official site, tax included) · wine pairing; a Japanese tea pairing (September 2026) · signature: cold mapo tofu, a tofu mousse topped with wagyu meat-miso and chili oil (2026 reviews) · a salad of 50–55 Ohara vegetables each cooked differently (August–September 2026) · examples: a "future" soupe de poisson of rare fish, with vegetables not sold at market, hamo and Matsutake as pasta, foie gras with black beans, ayu braised in red wine, lobster with Horikawa burdock, Sisteron lamb (October 2026); Akashi-fish dashi soup, corn soup with foie gras, Hino venison with pumpkin terrine, coconut panna cotta with a chili sorbet (September 2026); Tamura beef (October 2026) · ingredients the chef gathers personally: watercress from the Kamo River, game hunted in Niigata (Tabelog) · a gyoza shop and an online shop under the MOTOI name (official site)
places.notes: [French · Tomikoji-Nijo, a former Chinese-cuisine chef's French in a kimono merchant's house] A Taisho-era kimono merchant's house of about 100 years on Tomikoji-dori, renovated into a high-ceilinged dining room looking onto a courtyard garden. Chef Motoi Maeda, born in Kyoto in 1976, spent about ten years cooking Chinese food at a Kyoto hotel, then trained in Burgundy and at Pittoresque and HAJIME before opening here in 2012. The cooking is French with Chinese accents: a cold mapo tofu of tofu mousse, wagyu meat-miso and chili oil is the dish everyone mentions, alongside a salad of some 50 Ohara vegetables and condiments such as fermented black beans and dried shrimp. The chef forages watercress on the Kamo River and hunts game in Niigata. Courses change each visit, and the shop asks about previous visits when you book. Tabelog Award Bronze every year from 2019 to 2026. 2026 diners loved the room and the surprises; a few found the service thin. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

roles: Chef (Tabelog: "Chef Motoi Maeda"; official site: シェフ 前田元)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: as a child read cookbooks like picture books and cooked from them; after high school joined what is now RIHGA Royal Hotel Kyoto and worked about ten years as a Chinese-cuisine chef; moved to France and trained in Burgundy and other regions; after returning worked at Pittoresque in Kyoto and HAJIME in Osaka; opened MOTOI in the chef's hometown of Kyoto in January 2012. Tabelog says the chef judges heat by eye rather than with a thermometer and gathers wild watercress from the Kamo River. In September 2026 the chef came out to greet a lunch table. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2026; French WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Shukyaku ittai" (主客一体), a tea-ceremony phrase for host and guest creating the time together; MOTOI values the harmony (和) that guests and staff make together (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Cold mapo tofu; Ohara vegetable salad; French sauces with Chinese seasonings.

anecdotes.text: "The tofu had a mousse-like texture, and inside was Wagyu beef coated in a sauce. The fact that it was served cold was also a nice seasonal touch." — August 2026, first visit.
"When I added the fermented tofu sauce, dried shrimp, salted fish, and fermented black beans, it transformed the dish into something distinctly Chinese." — September 2026, Japanese tea pairing.
"The total with pairings was JPY 47,000." — October 2026, dinner.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (kyoto-motoi.com): Restaurant MOTOÏ、シェフ前田元のフィルターを通した新しいフレンチ、「主客一体のおもてなし」、ランチ Collection de Saison 13,200円 (約10品)、Gourmand 18,700円 (メインが牛肉、前菜にオマール海老)、ディナー Création 25,300円 (約13品)、特別室 (2〜8名) は限定メニューでランチ27,500円、ディナー46,200円、いずれも税込、別途サービス料10%、その日ごとにコースを用意するため予約時に食材のアレルギーや苦手なものを聞く、来店履歴も聞く、当日キャンセル100%、MOTOIの餃子のお店「モトイギョーザ」、通販。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019〜2026、フレンチ WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、富小路通二条下ル俵屋町186、大正時代の呉服商の邸宅を改装した一軒家、中庭、32席、個室あり、13歳未満不可、英語メニュー、英語を話せるスタッフ、ベジタリアンメニューあり、2012年1月31日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 冷たい麻婆豆腐、Ohara の50〜55種類の野菜のサラダ、中国料理の調味料、ワインペアリング、日本茶のペアリング、ペアリング込みで47,000円。

places.cuisine: Meat kaiseki: one monthly course of about 12–13 dishes built on brand wagyu — Omi beef from Okazaki Farm in Shiga, Kobe beef, Matsusaka beef (Tabelog) and, in 2026, Tajima beef from the producer Junya Ueda (May 2026) · Special Tajima Beef Course ¥60,000; with sukiyaki of Tajima ribeye ¥75,000 (Tabelog, from September 2026); plus 10% service · earlier 2026: "Omakase Short Course" ¥55,000 (August), Tajima beef course ¥55,000 with eight wines ¥25,000 (July) · fixtures: a clear consommé of shin, beef tongue sliced thin and cured on kombu with ponzu and salted kombu, "beef toro" sirloin sashimi, shabu-shabu, a charcoal-grilled sirloin or chateaubriand steak, sukiyaki, then rice with soy-marinated egg yolk, pickles and red miso soup (2026 reviews) · examples: white shrimp and beef tartare sushi with caviar, Tajima beef fried in beef fat with asparagus (May 2026); winter melon and sea urchin, Kamo eggplant and hairy crab (June 2026); Omi beef tartare and salmon roe on rice, Matsutake and chestnuts (October 2026) · a bitter "amer" pudding to finish · champagne, wine pairings and sake
places.notes: [Meat kaiseki · Gion, a self-taught owner's all-wagyu counter] A two-storey wooden house a step off Hanamikoji, reached down a narrow path between textured earthen walls, with eight seats at a hinoki counter (renovated in 2023). Owner Tsutomu Ito came to meat through a friend who graded beef and a first taste of beef butchered that same day, is self-taught as a cook, and opened in the owner's home town of Gion at the end of 2004 under the family name Miyoshi; the building had been the owner's mother's salon. One course a month runs through a dozen beef dishes — tongue cured on kombu, beef sashimi, shabu-shabu, steak and sukiyaki — between seasonal seafood and vegetables, and ends with rice and egg yolk. Tabelog Award 2026 Silver; a 2026 reviewer notes a Michelin star from 2018 to 2022. Upstairs is a one-group inn where diners can eat and then sleep. Expect ¥60,000–75,000 plus service; one July 2026 diner felt regulars got more attention.

roles: Owner (official site greeting; Waraku: 店主 伊藤力（いとうつとむ）)
CEO of Miyoshi Co., Ltd. (an August 2026 review, which writes the name "Chikara Ito")
chef_bio.origin: Gion, Kyoto (Tabelog: opened in the owner's home town of Gion).
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: an encounter with exceptionally fresh offal drew the owner to meat; the restaurant took the name Miyoshi, used in the family since a great-grandfather; the cooking is self-taught and has won a Michelin star. Per the official greeting: before opening, "the best meat craftsman" served the owner beef butchered that day, and that taste is the shop's starting point; it opened at the end of 2004 in Gion. Waraku web: the owner entered the meat world because a friend was a beef grader; self-taught; the shop opened in 2005 (as Waraku has it) in a building that was originally a salon run by the owner's mother. A May 2026 diner adds that the owner first worked in restaurant service and held a Michelin star from 2018 to 2022. The space was renovated in 2023; the second floor became an inn with its own counter (Tabelog), which the site calls THE MIYOSHI, one group a night. Serai (山本益博) also wrote up the shop, noting the owner talks through the beef at the counter. Tabelog Award 2026 Silver.
chef_bio.philosophy: "I want to create meat dishes nobody has seen yet", searching for new flavours "in conversation with the meat" every day; come hungry (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kombu-cured beef tongue; beef sashimi; shabu-shabu, steak and sukiyaki in one course.

anecdotes.text: "You can eat until you're full and then sleep right away. Isn't that the best?" — the owner on the upstairs inn (Tabelog).
"This shabu-shabu uses only the center cut of the rib, with the surrounding parts cut away." — May 2026; course ¥70,000 plus 10% service.
"It was nice that they asked if I wanted to add anything without needing to decide in advance." — June 2026, sukiyaki added mid-course.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (niku-miyoshi.com): にくの匠 三芳（みよし）、2004年末に京都・祇園で開業、開業前に最高の肉職人がその日にさばいた牛を食べさせてくれた「最高鮮度」の感動が原点、「今まで誰も見たことのない肉料理を創ってみたい」、日々肉と会話しながら新しい味を探求、お腹を空かせておいでください、旅館「THE MIYOSHI」(一組限定) で三芳でしか味わえない極上和牛懐石、東山区祇園町南側570-15、2部制 17:00/20:00、日曜定休、予約は電話 (12時〜23時、日曜を除く) と OMAKASE・TABLEALL (英語)・foodies-reserve、改装のため2023年1月3日〜6月30日休業。和樂web: 店主の伊藤力（いとうつとむ）さんは友人に肉の格付員がいたことから肉の世界へ、料理は独学、店は2005年開店、もとは伊藤さんの母が営むサロン。サライ.jp (山本益博): カウンター内で調理するご主人の伊藤さんが牛肉の話をしてくれる、上海蟹と牛肉とキャビアのお凌ぎ。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award 2026 Silver、Tajima beef の特別コース60,000円、すき焼き付き75,000円、サービス料10%、カウンター8席、中学生以上。口コミ(2026年5月〜10月): タン刺し、kombu で締めた牛タン、牛トロの刺身、しゃぶしゃぶ、ステーキ、すき焼き、卵黄の醤油漬けとご飯。

cultural_comfort.note: English booking through TABLEALL (official site); one set course at a counter; an October 2026 diner sat beside an overseas guest.

places.cuisine: Japanese omakase of about 12 dishes that borrows ingredients and methods from other countries — Chinese and "ethnic" touches on a ryotei and kappo base (Tabelog) · seasonal omakase course ¥30,250 at dinner or Saturday lunch (Tabelog, tax included), plus 10% service; with a wine pairing about ¥44,000 (August 2026) · July 2026: Okayama umeboshi with silken tofu purée, hairy crab with tomato jelly and white zuiki, sushi-rice porridge with turban shell and its liver and sea urchin, eel and Kamo eggplant soup with sansho, Akashi sea bream and octopus, fried ayu in fresh spring rolls with herbs, a Miyazaki-style cold soup with soba, salted rice balls topped with corn tempura, beef with a sauce, grilled warabi mochi with milk ice cream · September 2026: salmon roe on Kurosaki edamame rice porridge, a soup of dried Matsutake in round dashi, ayu with jumbo peanuts and vinegared pear; rice as sushi, as tamago-kake-gohan and as mapo rice · October 2026: an autumn "parfait" of fried spring-roll wrapper, tofu sauce, dashi jelly, figs, scallop and sweet shrimp; soba rice with dried Matsutake; guchi with new-rice purée · wine and sake chosen for the dishes
places.notes: [Kappo · Higashiyama, a ryotei-trained chef's playful counter] A second-floor counter of nine near Higashiyama station, where owner-chef Tsukasa Miyashita, from Mie and trained for sixteen years at Gion Maruyama and Gion Sasaki, cooks Japanese food with turns no one else takes: fried ayu wrapped in fresh spring rolls, a dried-Matsutake soup with a Chinese edge, an autumn "parfait" of tofu sauce and dashi jelly, rice served as sushi, as egg-on-rice and as mapo. Opened in 2021 with Yuumei Hongo, it holds a star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026 (per 2026 reviews) and Tabelog's 2026 Bronze. Everyone starts at 18:00; the room is lively, and a July 2026 diner was greeted at the door by the chef. Course ¥30,250 plus service; closed Sundays and Mondays.

roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog set menu: "our chef and owner, Tsukasa Miyashita")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section (written in the first person): born in 1985 in Mie, interested in cooking from childhood, studied at Tsuji Culinary Institute, then six years at Gion Maruyama and ten at Gion Sasaki; opened Higashiyama Tsukasa in 2021 together with Yuumei Hongo, met during training, drawing on both ryotei and kappo cooking under the idea of "cuisine not served elsewhere". Tabelog's introduction adds experience in innovative and Chinese cooking. Reviewers in 2026 greet "Tsukasa, Hongo, and Hiraku-kun" at the counter (September) and report one Michelin star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto & Osaka 2026 (August, October). Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Cuisine not served elsewhere"; delicious food and enjoyable experiences (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Ayu spring rolls; dried-Matsutake soup; rice in several forms.

anecdotes.text: "The chef personally welcomed us at the entrance, which was a nice touch." — July 2026, date night.
"The staff and customers here seem to have a great camaraderie, making it a fun place to be!" — July 2026.
"I also appreciated that I could enjoy rice in various forms, including sushi, tamago kake gohan (rice with raw egg), and mapo rice." — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Japanese omakase of vegetables, wild plants and flowers the owner gathers in Ohara and Miyama, with fish and a charcoal-grilled 50-day aged beef from the Kusatsu butcher Sakaeya, made for this shop (Tabelog) · omakase lunch ¥15,000; dinner ¥30,000 (Tabelog, tax included); a 5% service charge from 1 December · the course: a large hassun, white-miso soup, sashimi, grilled fish, a second soup, the aged beef, ayu, handmade 100% buckwheat soba, rice cooked in an okudo stove, then desserts (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · August 2026: a hassun with Ohara edamame, river goby tsukudani, Miyama venison, Akashi conger-eel pressed sushi; white miso with Ohara corn; conger-eel sashimi with Ohara cucumber; 50-day aged Kagoshima beef; ayu with Matsutake tempura; soba with clam broth; rice with free-range chicken · October 2026: white miso with Ohara pumpkin, Nagano Matsutake, Shiga soba with ayu, Hirakodori chicken rice with its egg yolk · natural sparkling water from Oku-Aizu and cold-brewed tea for non-drinkers; sake and wine
places.notes: [Kappo · Higashiyama, a forager's "museum of food" opposite Shoren-in] Across the lane from the gate of Shoren-in, behind a plaque reading Shun Gyuan and a tea-house approach, eight seats face a tatami-topped counter, an okudo stove and shelves of antique jars. Owner Masanori Tsukioka, from Hokkaido, began cooking at 15 in Sapporo, trained around Japan including under Hisao Nakahigashi at Kusakui Nakahigashi, ran Jimi Kougetsu in Kusatsu, and moved to the United States in 2019 to open a restaurant, but COVID ended the plan and the chef restarted in Kyoto, opening here in 2021. The course follows what the chef picks in Ohara and Miyama: a hassun like a summer meadow, white-miso soups, Akashi conger eel, 50-day aged beef from Sakaeya in Kusatsu, handmade 100% buckwheat soba and stove-cooked rice. Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze and Japanese cuisine WEST 100. Lunch ¥15,000, dinner ¥30,000; closed Tuesdays, Wednesdays and the last day of the month.

roles: Owner-chef (August 2026 review: "The owner, Masanori Tsukioka"; Tabelog: "the owner personally sources")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section (first person): born in 1976 in Hokkaido; began cooking at 15 at a local-cuisine restaurant in Sapporo; trained in Aichi, Kyoto, Tokyo and Shiga; moved to the United States in 2019 to open a restaurant, gave that up because of COVID and restarted in Kyoto; inspired by the owner of Kusakui Nakahigashi, met during training, to work in dialogue with nature, walking the mountains and fields. An August 2026 review adds that the chef trained under Hisao Nakahigashi at Kusakui Nakahigashi and ran Jimi Kougetsu in Kusatsu, Shiga, before Tsukioka, and gathers vegetables, wild plants and flowers in Ohara, Miyama and Kyoko. The aged beef comes from Sakaeya, a Kusatsu butcher (Tabelog). An October 2026 diner thanks "the head chef and the owner" for warm hospitality; another found the proprietress "very beautiful and elegant". Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "A museum of food": wabi-sabi in a traditional Japanese room, and dishes that express gratitude for nature's blessings (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Foraged Ohara and Miyama vegetables; 50-day aged beef; handmade 100% buckwheat soba; okudo-cooked rice.

anecdotes.text: "The table in front of me is not wooden but tatami-style. Interesting." — August 2026, dinner.
"Lunch was fully booked both times. It seems there were cancellations due to the typhoon, but the seats were still filled." — October 2026, a second visit.
"The sardine rice was enhanced by the rich yolk from the Hirako Chicken farm in Kobayashi City, Miyazaki Prefecture." — September 2026, ¥15,000 lunch.

Reservation only, online or by phone from 10:00, not during service; bookings open two months ahead to the day (official site). 26 seats: 4 at the counter, tables, and one private room for 5–6 (Tabelog; official site). No children under 6; at lunch, children 6–11 in the private room only; dinner from 12 (official site). No sandals or very casual clothes; no strong perfume (Tabelog; official site). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible; free Wi-Fi (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). Same-day cancellation 100% (official site). Opened 5 December 2014 (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Italian built on Kyoto vegetables and Japanese ingredients — Kujo green onion, Shogoin daikon, rapeseed flowers, wasabi; fish sometimes aged for days (Tabelog) · weekday lunch, 6 dishes and 2 desserts, ¥12,100; weekend and holiday lunch ¥16,940; lunch or dinner, 8 dishes and 3 desserts, ¥24,200 (Tabelog, tax included; the official menu page lists ¥12,100 and ¥21,780); service 10% (Tabelog) · extra pasta about ¥2,000 or risotto about ¥4,000 at lunch (August 2026) · official sample dinner: prosciutto with potato and yuzu kosho; gazpacho with sakura shrimp; tomato, new ginger, cutlassfish and coriander; asparagus, barley and squid; Kamigamo cucumber with retired-dairy-cow beef and sesame; Chinese chives, turban shell and chitarra · 2026 reviews: prosciutto with mango, passion fruit and dosa; ayu with tagliolini; Gifu Tada ham with bean mousse and ricotta; a vegan plate of cucumber, miso and melon (August); hamo soup reminiscent of tom yum with Manganji peppers and coriander, new-squid risotto (October); the meal ends with "cenci", small fried pastries · wines chosen by a sommelier; tea pairings for non-drinkers (official site; October 2026)
places.notes: [Italian · Shogoin, a Kyoto-born chef's Italian in a century-old house] Near Heian Shrine, down a narrow entrance and stairs that one diner likened to entering a cave, a renovated house of over 100 years with walls of twisted Meiji-style brickwork, Wajima lacquer and Kyoto ceramics on the table. Chef Ken Sakamoto, born in Kyoto in 1975, fell for Italian food on a university trip, trained at Il Papparaldo and spent nine years as head chef of Il Giottone before opening here in 2014. The courses pair Kyoto vegetables with fish and meat in surprising ways — prosciutto with mango and dosa, a hamo soup like tom yum — and the meal ends with cenci, the fried pastry that gives the shop its name; a vegan plate has appeared mid-course. Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026 one star (per 2026 reviews), Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze. Weekday lunch is ¥12,100; one October 2026 diner found the explanations hurried.

chef_bio.origin: Born and raised in Kyoto, 1975 (Tabelog chef section).
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in Kyoto in 1975, with a mother who was a fine cook and a family that liked eating out; a university trip to Italy led to cooking; three and a half years at Il Papparaldo, then moved to Il Giottone when chef Yasuhiro Sasajima went independent, and was head chef of the main restaurant for nine years; opened cenci in 2014. The house is over 100 years old, with walls in the Meiji-era "nejirimanpo" twisted brickwork, woodwork by Japanese craftsmen, Wajima lacquerware, Kyoto ceramics and Ryusen knives (Tabelog). 2026 reviewers report one Michelin star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka 2026 (August). Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients first: local produce from Kyoto and around Japan, at their peak or aged to their best, combined in Italian dishes "you won't find anywhere else" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Kyoto vegetables in Italian courses; handmade pasta; the fried pastry "cenci".

anecdotes.text: "The dessert at the end, called 'Cenci,' is a type of fried pasta snack, which was a delightful palate cleanser in small bites." — September 2026, second visit.
"As I descended the stairs, I felt as if I was entering a cave, revealing a space that was unimaginable from the outside." — August 2026.
"Not only were the dishes delightful, but the tea pairings were also wonderful." — October 2026, dinner course at lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (cenci-kyoto.com): cenci チェンチ、左京区聖護院円頓美町44-7、ランチ12:00 (L.O.)〜15:00、ディナー18:00〜18:30 (L.O.)〜21:30、毎週月曜日と不定で火曜日・日曜日休み、ランチ21,780円 (8皿とデザート3皿、ディナーと同じ) と12,100円 (6皿とデザート2皿)、ディナー21,780円 (税サ込)、ある日のディナー: ペルシュウ、じゃがいも、柚子胡椒、ガスパチョ、桜海老、花穂紫蘇、トマト、新生姜、太刀魚、パクチー、上賀茂胡瓜、経産牛、胡麻、ニラ、サザエ、キタッラなど、料理に合わせたお茶も、予約は2か月先の同日まで、予約時にアレルギーや苦手な食材を知らせて、小学生未満は不可、ディナーは中学生未満不可、個室は5〜6名、当日キャンセル100%。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2025、平日ランチ12,100円、土日祝ランチ16,940円、24,200円 (ディナーと同じ)、サービス料10%、26席、2014年12月5日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 最後の小菓子が cenci、新烏賊のリゾット、動物性のものを使わない一皿、お茶のペアリング、ミシュランガイド京都・大阪2026で一つ星。

places.name: 竹屋町 三多 (Takeyamachi Mita)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. A set Japanese course seasoned with soy sauce and miso; 2026 courses included fried spring rolls, an asparagus tempura, somen noodles and sushi.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-led kaiseki course built on dashi, with soft-shelled turtle and beef in some dishes (2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Tabelog lists daily 16:00–22:00 with irregular closing days and asks guests to check; one dinner sitting a night, which 2026 diners report starting at 16:00 (September, a Saturday) or 18:00 (October) (Tabelog; reviews). Reservation only, online (Tabelog); hard to book, though cancellations open up on reservation sites (2026 reviews; a September 2026 diner booked through OMAKASE). Some autumn nights are private Matsutake gatherings (October 2026). 6 counter seats; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Opened 11 September 2010 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Takeyamachi, on a quiet street just south of the Imperial Palace — 5 min from the Kawaramachi-Marutamachi bus stop, 10 min from Jingu-Marutamachi, Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae or Marutamachi Stn
places.cuisine: One seasonal kaiseki course a night, on historic tableware (2026 reviews) · seasonal course ¥67,000 (September 2026); the autumn Matsutake gathering ¥75,000 including tax and drinks (October 2026); diners report ¥50,000–79,999 (Tabelog) · August 2026: egg tofu with Yura sea urchin sauce, stick sushi of Awaji horse mackerel with young ginger, steamed Setouchi abalone with fried asparagus and liver sauce, Akashi sea bream, hamo in white miso, charcoal-grilled Ariake eel, eggplant with soft-shelled-turtle sauce, sudachi somen, then three corn rices (plain, butter, black pepper) · September 2026: salmon roe with yam, Matsutake spring rolls, Akashi horse mackerel sushi, hamo with miso, grilled white sweet sea bream, hairy crab, abalone and eggplant in turtle broth, Matsutake clay-pot rice · October 2026: Matsutake spring rolls with dried sea-cucumber roe, Awaji mackerel sushi, sea bream with kombu and sea urchin, grilled cutlassfish with Matsutake, chateaubriand with chestnut flour and sansho, Matsutake rice · sake such as "Kuro-ryu" (as an October 2026 review writes it)
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Teramachi-Marutamachi, six seats and one sitting a night] A pure Japanese room of straw-flecked earthen walls and a single slab of keyaki for a counter that seats six, on a quiet street south of the Imperial Palace. Chef Hiroyuki Mita cooks one seasonal course for everyone and explains each dish; diners in 2026 single out the horse-mackerel and mackerel sushi, hamo in white miso, Matsutake spring rolls and the clay-pot rices at the end, all on old and notable tableware. The chef greets guests at the door and sees them off, a woman owner looks after the drinks, and reviewers call the service warm and unstuffy. Tabelog Silver every year from 2019 to 2026 and Japanese cuisine WEST 100. Hard to book; watch reservation sites for cancellations. Expect ¥60,000–79,999.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hiroyuki Mita (romaji from a September 2026 review; the kanji of the given name is not in a source)
roles: Head chef (September 2026 review: "the Japanese cuisine crafted by Chef Hiroyuki Mita")
The owner is a woman who serves the drinks (October 2026 review: "The owner is attentive to the drinks behind the counter, and her friendly and gentle demeanor is reassuring")
chef_bio.background: Opened 11 September 2010 (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2026 describe the head chef as humble and polite, explaining each dish (October), and "Mr. Mita himself" waiting at the entrance to welcome guests (August); an August 2026 diner was also struck by the proprietress's attentive hospitality. The room has walls of diatomaceous earth mixed with straw and a single-piece keyaki counter (October 2026). Tabelog Award Silver 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.specialty: Horse-mackerel and mackerel sushi; hamo in white miso; Matsutake in autumn; clay-pot rice.

anecdotes.text: "Upon arriving at the restaurant, Mr. Mita himself was standing at the entrance, graciously welcoming me." — August 2026, booked on a lucky opening.
"The aroma of the matsutake was so strong that it reached even the distant tables." — October 2026, a second visit.
"The cost was JPY 75,000 per person (tax included, with drinks included at a very reasonable price)." — October 2026, Matsutake event.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 竹屋町 三多、日本料理、中京区寺町通竹屋町下ル久遠院前町667-1、16:00〜22:00、不定休、予約はネットで、カウンター6席、貸切20名まで、禁煙、カード可、2010年9月11日オープン、The Tabelog Award Silver 2019〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 鱧白味噌、松茸ご飯 (日本語の写真説明)、鯵や鯖の寿司、Matsutake の春巻き、最後に土鍋ご飯、歴史ある器、店主と大将の温かいもてなし、予約が取りにくい、季節のコース67,000円、松茸の会75,000円 (税・飲み物込み)。

cultural_comfort.note: One set course at a six-seat counter; booked online; dishes are explained in Japanese by the chef.

places.name: 未在 (Mizai)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the official site says the shop confirms portion size and allergies when you reserve. No gluten information; a long tea-kaiseki course with many dishes seasoned with soy sauce and miso.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a tea-kaiseki course of sashimi, fish, meat and hamo, built on dashi (2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: One sitting a night: doors from about 17:30, everyone starts at 18:00 (arrive by 17:45) and the meal takes about three hours (official site; Tabelog); 2026 diners report anything from under 2.5 hours to near midnight. Closed Wednesday and irregularly (Tabelog). Reservation by phone, up to a year ahead; the phone is hard to reach during service and an hour either side (official site; Tabelog). The shop confirms a week before; cancellation 50% from seven days before, 100% from five days, and no date changes in that period (official site). Smart casual or better, kimono welcome; children from middle-school age (official site). 14 counter seats and a tea room as a private room (Tabelog; official site). Payment basically cash, though cards are accepted (official site; Tabelog lists VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX). Photos of the food are not allowed (2026 reviews). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened June 2004; the site marked 22 years in June 2026. Relocated within Maruyama-cho from 620-1 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Inside Maruyama Park beyond Yasaka Shrine, at the far end of the park; the entrance is easy to miss — 15 min on foot from Gion-Shijo (Keihan) or Kawaramachi (Hankyu)
places.cuisine: Tea kaiseki in the house style (未在流献立): it opens with rice and a soup bowl as in a tea meal, moves through generous sashimi with many condiments, fish, meat and hamo, then a large hassun, a scorched-rice tea porridge, a big spread of fruit and matcha whisked by the owner (official site; 2026 reviews) · cuisine charge ¥65,000 plus tax and 10% service; market price in January and October; the tea room (private room) ¥35,000 extra (official site); Tabelog lists the "Mizairyu tea kaiseki" at ¥78,000 including tax · portions are famously large; diners are told to come hungry, and many leave some (2026 reviews) · an original sake made with the Kyoto rice Iwai (September 2026); wine, priced on asking (June 2026) · a house blend of eight spices, "八味", ¥2,000 a bottle or ¥3,500 for two, ordered by phone (official site)
places.notes: [Tea kaiseki · Maruyama Park, a Kyoto master's one-sitting counter] At the far end of Maruyama Park, beyond Yasaka Shrine, fourteen guests sit at one counter and start together at 18:00 for about three hours of tea kaiseki. The owner, Hitoshi Ishihara (石原仁司), born in Shimane in 1952, began training at 15 at a famous Osaka restaurant, rose to head chef in Kyoto at 24, and opened Mizai in 2004; a June 2026 reviewer recalls three Michelin stars many times over. The name is a Zen phrase: the way is never finished. The evening opens with the etiquette of a tea meal, then relaxes; it runs through a lavish sashimi course, a grand hassun, a scorched-rice tea porridge and an astonishing fruit course, and ends with matcha the owner whisks. No food photos. ¥65,000 plus tax and service, cash preferred; book by phone up to a year ahead.

roles: Owner (official site: "未在 主人　石原仁司")
chef_bio.background: Per a June 2026 review: born in 1952 in Shimane; joined the Osaka main restaurant of "Kichijo" (the review's spelling) at 15 and trained under its founder, Teiichi Yuki; head chef of its Kyoto restaurant at 24 and executive chef at 38; opened Mizai in Maruyama Park in 2004; the name comes from a Zen phrase meaning training never ends; three Michelin stars "multiple times". The official site's greeting (August 2026) marks 22 years since opening in June 2004, says the way is "still half-travelled", and offers a house eight-spice blend as an anniversary gift. A September 2026 diner first saw the owner on the NHK programme "Professional" about ten years earlier. Reviewers in 2026 describe the owner as strict and dignified at first, explaining tea-meal etiquette, then increasingly friendly; apprentices greet guests and explain dishes. Tabelog Award Silver 2019–2023, Bronze 2024–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "一座建立": a fine shared time through the spirit of tea kaiseki, which also asks guests to show consideration for one another (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Tea kaiseki in the Mizai style; the hassun; the closing fruit; matcha.

anecdotes.text: "Come after skipping breakfast and lunch. This is no joke; it's a technical necessity." — June 2026, a third visit.
"I felt relieved when I was told I could enjoy the dishes in my preferred way starting from the second course." — June 2026; about ¥130,000 per person with wine.
"Ishihara-san initially comes across as dignified, but he becomes increasingly friendly as the meal progresses." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (mizai.jp): 御料理 未在、主人 石原仁司、2026年6月で開店22周年 (令和八年 葉月の御挨拶)、未だ道半ば、周年記念に主人好みの香辛料「八味」(1本2,000円税込、2本3,500円)、皆様一斉に18時開始、茶懐石 (未在流献立) に約3時間、お料理代六万五千円 (税別)、サービス料10%別、一月と十月は時価、茶室代 (個室) 三万五千円 (税別)、支払いは基本的に現金 (カード可)、予約は一年前から、営業時間中 (前後1時間含む) は電話が繋がりにくい、お食事の量やアレルギー等を確認、1週間前に連絡、キャンセル料は7日前50%・5日前100%、スマートカジュアル以上 (和装含む)、「一座建立」、子どもは中学生以上。食べログ (店舗会員): 未在、日本料理、東山区八坂鳥居前東入ル円山町613 円山公園、水曜休み・不定休、カウンター14席と個室、The Tabelog Award Silver 2019〜2023・Bronze 2024〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、円山町620-1から移転。口コミ(2026年5月〜9月): 料理の写真は不可、最初に茶懐石の作法の説明、量が多い、お造り、八寸、おこげの茶粥、果物、主人が点てる抹茶。

cultural_comfort.note: Book by phone; one set course with tea-meal etiquette explained at the start; no food photos; smart casual or better.

places.name: 八寸 (Hassun)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. An omakase kaiseki seasoned with soy sauce and miso; 2026 courses included sea bream with sea-urchin soy sauce, a Yawata roll, simmered fried tofu and grilled fish with miso.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seasonal kaiseki built on dashi, with hamo, eel, duck and other fish (2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Lunch Tue–Sat 12:00–13:00 (last order 13:00); dinner Mon–Sat 18:00–21:00; closed Sunday (Tabelog). Reservations online until the day before (Tabelog); Ikkyu and Tabelog bookings reported (2026 reviews). 18 seats: a 12-seat counter and a sunken-kotatsu private room for 6 (Tabelog). Children welcome; call to book with children (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Founded in 1945 (September 2026 review).
places.neighborhood: Gion, through a stone-paved passage behind a plain noren — 5 min from Gion-Shijo Stn (Keihan), 8 min from Kawaramachi (Hankyu)
places.cuisine: Omakase kaiseki from a second-generation Gion kitchen, with natural hamo in summer and Tanba Matsutake in autumn (Tabelog) · omakase kaiseki lunch ¥13,200; dinner ¥27,500 (Tabelog, tax included) · lunch in September–October 2026: steamed fig with sesame sauce or sesame tofu, a hassun (river goby, hamo roe, Yawata roll, sweet potato, smoked egg yolk), tuna and sea-bream sashimi, a dobin-mushi of hamo and Matsutake, grilled sawara, seasoned or Matsutake rice, pickles and fruit · dinner in October 2026: yuba steamed with maitake and koutake, duck loin, seared hamo, sea bream with sea-urchin soy sauce, the season's last Matsutake and hamo dobin-mushi, charcoal-grilled sawara with black Manganji pepper and miso, crab in vinegar, wild eel from Mie grilled over charcoal · sake
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, a family kaiseki house since 1945] Through a simple noren and a stone-paved passage in the middle of Gion, a long, polished hinoki counter of twelve and a sunken-kotatsu room at the back. The restaurant was founded in 1945; the chef now is Kanji Kubota, born in Kyoto Prefecture in 1976, who trained in Tokyo and came home to take over from the chef's father, who still appears now and then. The cooking is quiet and seasonal — hamo in summer, Matsutake dobin-mushi in autumn, a hassun on artists' tableware — and lunch is ¥13,200. New guests are called by name, and in September 2026 an apprentice explained dishes in fluent English to overseas diners. Tabelog Bronze or Silver every year since 2019 and Japanese cuisine WEST 100. Closed Sundays.

roles: Chef and owner, second generation (Tabelog: "the second generation of 'Hassun'"; "only ingredients that both the owner and his father ... agree upon")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1976 in Kyoto Prefecture; trained in Tokyo, then returned to Kyoto; with little wish to be a chef at first, was encouraged by regular customers to take over the restaurant run by the father, and now stands in the kitchen as the second generation; the father and son choose the ingredients together, and the tableware is by contemporary artists the chef collects. Tabelog's English gives the father's name as both "Masaru Kubota" and "Mamoru Kubota"; no kanji is given. A September 2026 diner reports a founding in 1945, the chef aged 51, and the father appearing occasionally. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019 and 2021–2026, Silver 2020; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasoning that brings out the ingredients' own flavour (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal hassun; hamo; Matsutake dobin-mushi.

anecdotes.text: "The Japanese and overseas guests were separated, and the overseas guests were given fluent explanations in English by an apprentice." — September 2026, lunch.
"Even new customers are greeted by name, making it an easy place to enter alone." — September 2026.
"I spent two and a half hours enjoying my meal while chatting with the chef." — October 2026, dinner.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 八寸、日本料理、東山区祇園末吉町95、京阪祇園四条駅から徒歩5分、昼は火〜土 12:00〜13:00、夜は月〜土 18:00〜21:00、日曜休み、おまかせ懐石 昼13,200円・夜27,500円 (税込)、18席 (カウンター12、足を下ろせる個室6名)、子ども可、The Tabelog Award Bronze・Silver、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月、写真説明は日本語): 舞茸、こうたけの湯葉蒸し、鴨ロース、鱧の焼き霜、マグロと鯛 (鯛はウニ醤油で)、今年ラストの松茸と鱧の土瓶蒸し、サワラの炭焼き 黒万願寺唐辛子 お味噌添え、蟹の酢の物、三重の天然のうなぎの炭焼き、海外の客には弟子が英語で説明、初めての客も名前で呼ばれる。

cultural_comfort.note: An apprentice explained dishes to overseas guests in fluent English (September 2026); book online until the day before.

places.name: 大市 (Daiichi)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free as served: there is one dish, and its broth is turtle, sake, soy sauce and ginger (a July 2026 diner asked); no gluten-free version is mentioned.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the only dish is soft-shelled turtle hot pot, then rice porridge with egg.
places.hours_raw: Lunch from 12:00 (last entry 12:30); dinner in two sittings from 17:00 (last entry 17:30) and 19:00 (last entry 19:30); closed Tuesday (may change), a summer break from late July to early August, and over the New Year (Tabelog). Reservation only (Tabelog). 12 seats at tables, and tatami private rooms for 2 to 20 (Tabelog); some meals are served side by side in a private room off a courtyard (July 2026). No children (Tabelog). The dining rooms are non-smoking; smoking is allowed in the entrance area (Tabelog). Parking for 6 cars (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; no service charge, as it is included in the course (Tabelog). A taxi from the centre costs about ¥1,300; Kitano-Hakubaicho Stn (Randen) is about 18 minutes on foot (Tabelog; July 2026 review). The official site is down for maintenance (November 2026).
places.neighborhood: Kamigyo, where Shimonaga-cho street (as a June 2026 review spells it) meets Senbon-dori — about 18 min on foot from Kitano-Hakubaicho Stn, or a taxi
places.cuisine: One dish, soft-shelled turtle "marunabe", in a set course: a small dish of turtle jelly or simmered turtle with ginger, the hot pot served twice (different cuts each time), then rice porridge with rice, mochi and eggs, pickles and seasonal fruit (2026 reviews) · course ¥26,000 including tax and service, lunch or dinner; extra hot pot from ¥10,600 per person; porridge refills offered (Tabelog) · the pot is cooked fast over coke in thick custom clay pots from Shigaraki that take on flavour over years (July 2026); diners were told of a heat of 1,600 degrees (July, September 2026) · drinks: beer and sake, priced on the bill (two beers and two sake ¥8,000, October 2026)
places.notes: [Suppon · Kamigyo, a 340-year-old turtle house] An Edo-period building on a quiet street near Senbon-dori, with a courtyard and tatami rooms, where one family has served a single dish for about 340 years and eighteen generations, by diners' accounts since the Genroku era. Sword marks said to be left by samurai remain at the entrance (July 2026), and reviewers note that writers such as Yasunari Kawabata and Naoya Shiga were patrons. The course never changes: turtle jelly, the bubbling marunabe of turtle, sake, soy sauce and ginger served twice, then a rich rice porridge with mochi and egg. Fans call it odourless and deeply savoury; one 2026 diner found the repeated pot monotonous, another the pace brisk. ¥26,000 all in; no children; parking for six.

chef_bio.background: A soft-shelled turtle specialist said by 2026 reviewers to be about 340 years old (founded in the Genroku era) and in its eighteenth generation, with the building kept as it was in the Edo period, including sword marks at the entrance said to be from samurai (July and August 2026 reviews). An August 2026 reviewer names Yasunari Kawabata and Naoya Shiga among past patrons and describes the round Kyoto fans given by maiko and geiko that hang in the house. A server portions the hot pot at the table (August, October 2026). Tabelog Award Bronze 2021–2026. No owner is named in a source read.
chef_bio.specialty: Soft-shelled turtle marunabe; turtle rice porridge.

anecdotes.text: "When I asked what was in it, I found out it was just turtle, Japanese sake, soy sauce, and ginger." — July 2026, private room.
"It retains the same appearance since its founding, with even sword marks said to be made by samurai remaining at the entrance." — July 2026.
"The same hot pot dish was served twice in the course, which made me quite tired of eating." — July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (suppon-daiichi.com): すっぽん 大市、ショッピングサイトは一時停止中 (2026年11月)。食べログ: 大市、すっぽん・日本料理・鍋、上京区六番町364、昼12:00 (最終入店12:30)、夜は17:00 (最終入店17:30) と19:00 (最終入店19:30) の2部、火曜休み、夏季休暇 (7月下旬〜8月上旬) と年末年始、予約のみ、テーブル12席と個室、子ども不可、駐車場6台、サービス料なし (コース料金内に込み)、すっぽん鍋と zosui が中心のコースは昼夜とも1人26,000円 (税込)、追加は1人10,600円から、zosui のおかわりも、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2021〜2026。口コミ(2026年6月〜10月): 約340年、18代、marunabe を2回、zosui、Shigaraki の土鍋とコークスの火 (英語の口コミ)、生姜、Yasunari Kawabata や Naoya Shiga も通った。

cultural_comfort.note: One fixed course, so there is nothing to order but drinks; staff serve the hot pot at the table.
