places.name: 草喰 なかひがし (Soujiki Nakahigashi)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking (by phone, in Japanese, or through the foreign-language booking site). No gluten information. Vegetables and wild plants lead, but the set course includes tempura in spring (official site), and dishes are seasoned with soy sauce and miso.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the course is plant-led but built on dashi, with charcoal-grilled fish, dried sardines (mezashi) with the rice, and in 2026 also ayu, carp, eel, venison and wagyu (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Lunch entry 12:00–13:00, dinner entry 18:00–19:00 (official site; Tabelog lists 12:00–14:00 and 18:00–21:00). Closed Monday (holidays included), alternate Tuesdays (ask) and the last day of each month (official site; Tabelog says the last Tuesday of the month). Reservations by phone from 8:00 on the 1st of the month before (the next day if the 1st is a closing day); phone bookings are in Japanese only, and the site links an online booking site for other languages (official site). Hard to book: a September 2026 diner called for 30 minutes. 30 seats: 12 at the counter and two tatami rooms upstairs for 2–6 (Tabelog; official site). Children from upper elementary school; smart casual, no flip-flops or beachwear (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog). Cash or credit cards (official site); Tabelog also lists transit IC cards. A 22-minute walk from Demachiyanagi Stn, or 3 minutes from the Ginkakuji-michi bus stop (official site).
places.neighborhood: Jodoji, Sakyo, at the start of the approach to Ginkaku-ji — 3 min from the Ginkakuji-michi bus stop; 10 min by car from Demachiyanagi Stn
places.cuisine: Wild plants, flowers and vegetables the owner gathers each morning in Ohara, in a set course: a hassun like a scene from the hills, soups, simply grilled dishes, then rice cooked in a wood-fired okudo-san stove with grilled dried sardines and pickles, refills free (official site; Tabelog) · lunch from ¥12,100, dinner from ¥24,200 including tax and service (official site); from 1 April 2026 lunch from ¥10,000 and dinner from ¥20,000 before tax and service (official notice) · extras at a charge, such as Matsutake rice +¥4,000 (September 2026) or tamago-kake-gohan (October 2026) · September 2026 lunch: a hassun on a lotus leaf, ayu with uruka, summer venison with autumn vegetables, Matsutake rice topped with karasumi · October 2026: Matsutake with soft-shelled turtle, carp sashimi, grilled eel, roast wagyu, bamboo-shoot rice; okoge and ochazuke at the end · sake such as Eiketsu and Shinsei (October 2026)
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Ginkaku-ji, a forager's kitchen of wild plants and stove-cooked rice] At the foot of the approach to Ginkaku-ji, a counter of twelve and two upstairs tatami rooms where the course is whatever Hisao Nakahigashi found that morning in Ohara: shoots, leaves, flowers and seeds, in a hassun laid out like a hillside, soups and plainly grilled dishes. Born in Kyoto Prefecture in 1952 and raised at Miyamasou, the inn in Hanase known for tsumikusa (foraged-plant) cooking, the owner trained there, served as its head chef and opened here in 1997; the rice, cooked in an okudo-san wood stove and served with grilled dried sardines, became the main event after the 1993 rice shortage. The site reports a Michelin Green Star for its sustainable approach. Diners love the chef's jokes at the counter; book by phone from 8:00 on the 1st of the month before. Lunch from ¥12,100, dinner from ¥24,200 all in.

roles: Owner and representative (official site: 代表 中東久雄; Tabelog: "owner of Kusakui Nakahigashi")
chef_bio.origin: Kyoto Prefecture, born 1952; raised at Miyamasou in Hanase (Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1952 in Kyoto Prefecture and raised at Miyamasou, a traditional inn in Hanase known for tsumikusa cooking; after high school trained under its previous head, Kichiji Nakahigashi, the originator of tsumikusa cooking (a September 2026 review gives "Yoshitsugu Nakahigashi"); head chef at Miyamasou, then opened this restaurant in 1997 (a September 2026 review says 1996). In the 1993 rice shortage a clay rice pot from Ichishiro-gama in Hikone led to the house style with plain white rice as the main dish. Every morning the owner goes to Ohara to gather wild plants and seasonal produce (Tabelog; official site). The official site's message from 中東久雄 cites the motto "eat everything that can be eaten" and a Michelin Green Star for its sustainable approach; the site also carries a message from 中東克之, whose role is not stated. In October 2026 one diner visited on a day the head chef was away. Tabelog Award Gold 2020, Silver 2019, 2021–2023 and 2025, Bronze 2024 and 2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025. Tabelog's English spells the name Kusajiki, Kusakui and Sojiki; the shop's own domain is soujiki-nakahigashi.jp.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Eat everything that can be eaten": gratitude for every life the sun and water raise, and no waste, down to radish and carrot peel and roots (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Foraged wild plants from Ohara; the hassun; okudo-san rice with grilled dried sardines.

anecdotes.text: "As always, I was introduced to new ingredients, including a type of 'grass' I had never heard of before." — September 2026; about three visits a year.
"After 30 minutes of continuous calling, I finally got through and secured a lunch slot." — September 2026.
"The rice was cooked in an okudo (traditional stove)! It was glossy and sweet." — October 2026, lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (soujiki-nakahigashi.jp): 草喰なかひがし、運営会社 有限会社草喰なかひがし、代表 中東久雄、左京区浄土寺石橋町32-3、入店時間12:00〜13:00・18:00〜19:00、定休日は月曜日・隔週火曜日 (要問合せ)・月の最終日、現金・各種クレジット、予約は毎月1日の午前8時から翌月分を電話で (日本語のみ、外国語は予約サイト)、お昼のコース12,100円〜・夜のコース24,200円〜 (税・サ込)、2026年4月1日から昼10,000円〜・夜20,000円〜 (税・サ別)、京都・大原の山々から採集した山菜や野菜、八寸、炭火で焼いた肴、お竃さんご飯とめざし、ご飯のおかわり自由、大将の軽快なトーク、2階の個室、「食べられるものはすべて食べ尽くす」、ミシュラングリーンスター、銀閣寺道バス停から徒歩3分。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Gold 2020 ほか、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、30席 (カウンター12、2階に座敷2室)、小学校高学年から、スマートカジュアル。口コミ(2026年9月〜10月): 松茸とすっぽん (日本語の写真説明)、ayu、鹿、karasumi をのせた Matsutake ご飯、めざしと漬物、電話予約がつながりにくい。

cultural_comfort.note: Phone bookings are in Japanese only; the official site links a booking site for other languages. One set course; the chef talks with guests at the counter.

places.name: IL GARAGE (イル ガラージュ)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the shop asks for allergies in advance and may not manage changes on the day (official site; Tabelog). No gluten information; handmade pasta such as bigoli is a house specialty, and bread and cannoli are part of the course (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: one seasonal course with fish, duck, beef and, in autumn and winter, game; apart from allergies the shop does not change ingredients for dislikes (official site; Tabelog).
places.hours_raw: Lunch from 12:00 on Saturday and Sunday; dinner from 18:00; closed Wednesday and occasionally (Tabelog). The lunch course takes about 2.5 hours and dinner about 3 (Tabelog). Reservation only, by the day before, for just two groups per sitting; five or more take the whole room (Tabelog). 8 seats at two round tables (Tabelog). No children (Tabelog). Up a flight of stairs, no lift (Tabelog). Please keep phones out of the way during the meal (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog; official site). Opened 17 December 2018 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Sakaimachi-dori below Sanjo, on the second floor above a garage — 7 min from Karasuma Oike Stn, 9 min from Karasuma/Shijo Stn
places.cuisine: A seasonal course of Italian regional cooking with "a pinch of creativity", built on Japanese produce (official site; Tabelog) · lunch course ¥13,200 plus service (February 2026); diners report about ¥16,000 at lunch and ¥20,000–39,999 at dinner (2026 reviews) · bigoli, the thick Veneto pasta, made fresh every morning; Sicilian cannoli filled with sweet shrimp, home-made karasumi and sudachi purée as a starter (Tabelog) · February 2026 lunch: home-made ham with strawberries; Wakayama squid with puntarelle; Mie flounder with celeriac; Ibaraki whitebait pasta with cima di rapa; Nanatani duck with tartiflette; charcoal-grilled Kumamoto red beef; butterbur-bud ice cream; bonet · July 2026: cod with bottarga, beef prosciutto on Pione grapes, horse mackerel · game in autumn and winter (Tabelog) · an extensive wine list, with drinks recommended by Midori (July 2026)
places.notes: [Italian · Sakaimachi-Sanjo, a couple's two-table dining room above a garage] Up the stairs over a garage on Sakaimachi-dori, two round tables and one sitting at lunch and at dinner, run by Masato and Midori Shirakawa, who met at a Kyoto Italian restaurant, married and spent 2009–2014 cooking and serving in Italy at Locanda San Lorenzo (Belluno), La Torre del Saracino (Naples) and La Madia (Agrigento). Masato cooks; Midori makes the desserts and runs the room and the wine. The course follows the season with Italian regional dishes and a light creative touch: bigoli rolled each morning, sweet-shrimp cannoli, duck, charcoal-grilled beef, game in winter. Tabelog likens it to being invited into the Shirakawas' home. Tabelog Bronze 2025 and 2026, Italian WEST 100. Book by the day before; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Masato Shirakawa; Midori Shirakawa (official site: "Masato e Midori Shirakawa")
roles: Midori: desserts and service (Tabelog: "Midori takes care of desserts and service")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: Masato met Midori, who handled service at the Kyoto Italian restaurant where Masato was training; the two married and went to Italy together to learn regional cooking in Veneto, Naples and Sicily, then opened in 2018 after five years in Italy. The official site lists 2009–2014 at Locanda San Lorenzo (one star, Belluno), La Torre del Saracino (two stars, Naples) and La Madia (two stars, Agrigento). The chef was drawn in Italy to modern cooking rooted in tradition (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2026 note the husband cooks every dish and the wife recommends drinks (July). The owners want a relaxed room rather than a tense one (Tabelog). Tabelog Award Bronze 2025, 2026; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Semplice, ma con un pizzico di fantasia": Italian regional cooking with a pinch of creativity, and the Italy the couple lived in for five years (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Bigoli made each morning; sweet-shrimp cannoli; seasonal Italian courses.

anecdotes.text: "The chef, who is the husband, prepares all the dishes himself, while his wife provides detailed recommendations for drinks in the dining area." — July 2026, lunch.
"True to its name, it's located above a garage." — August 2026, dinner booked two days ahead.
"The lunch course is priced at JPY 13,200 (service charge not included)." — February 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ilgaragekyoto.com): IL GARAGE -イル ガラージュ-、ガレージの二階、テーブル2卓だけのレストラン、日本の旬の食材を季節を感じるコース仕立てに、イタリア地方料理とひと摘みの創造性、夫婦で5年を過ごしたイタリアを表現したい、Masato e Midori Shirakawa、2009〜2014 Locanda San Lorenzo* (Belluno)、La Torre del Saracino** (Napoli)、La Madia** (Agrigento)、アレルギーは事前に、当日の変更は対応しかねる場合がある、秋冬はジビエ、苦手な食材には基本的に対応できない、サービス料10%、道祐町147 2F。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2025・2026、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2023・2025、昼は土日12:00〜、夜18:00〜、水曜と不定休、昼夜2組限定、前日までに予約、8席 (2卓)、子ども不可、エレベーターなし、2018年12月17日オープン。口コミ(2026年1月〜10月): ピオーネの上に牛の生ハム (日本語の写真説明)、夫が料理、妻がサービスとデザート、ランチ13,200円 (サービス料別)。

cultural_comfort.note: One set course; book by the day before; plate messages can be written in Italian (Tabelog).

places.name: El Tesoro (エル・テソロ)
places.gf_detail: Ask. A cocktail and whisky bar; spirits and fresh-fruit cocktails are the likelier choices. The home-made cakes (Basque cheesecake, chocolate and cinnamon cakes) are not described either way.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Fresh-fruit cocktails and spirits may suit; cheesecake and other cakes likely contain dairy and egg.
places.hours_raw: 16:00–1:00 (last entry 0:00, last order 0:30); closing days irregular, posted monthly — in November 2026 the 1st, 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th (official site); Tabelog lists Wednesdays closed. Reservations for 16:00–18:00, and after 18:00 up to 30 minutes before arriving; seats are limited, so call ahead (official site). Table charge ¥1,000 per person (Tabelog). A designated smoking bar (喫煙目的店, official site). 12 seats: 8 at the counter, a table for 4 that can be a private room (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR payments; no e-money (Tabelog). Opened 22 November 2006 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Yamato-oji below Sanjo, Yamato Bldg 1F, near Shinbashi in Gion — 4 min from Gion-Shijo Stn, 5 min from Sanjo Stn
places.cuisine: A cocktail and whisky bar: original cocktails made to your taste, with seasonal fresh-fruit cocktails the draw (official site; 2026 reviews) · examples: passion fruit, grape, watermelon with a salt rim, espresso martini, martini with large olives, Tanqueray gimlet, sidecar, screwdriver, a "Sky Ball" in a mug (July–October 2026) · whiskies including vintage bottles and Ardbeg An Oa (August, October 2026) · home-made cakes with the drinks: Basque cheesecake, chocolate cake, cinnamon cake, a dessert with a coffee cocktail (July–August 2026) · table charge ¥1,000; diners spend about ¥3,000–9,999 (2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Bar · Gion-Shinbashi, fruit cocktails and cake in a smoking bar] A polished counter of eight and soft jazz on the ground floor of the Yamato Building, a few minutes from Gion-Shijo station. The name is Spanish for treasure. The master, who a July 2026 reviewer says holds sommelier, sake and cheese qualifications, builds cocktails around whatever fruit is in season and will make one to your taste; diners pair them with home-made cakes or a vintage whisky. Diners in 2026 call the master kind and easy to talk to, which makes it a good first authentic bar. It is a designated smoking bar. One August 2026 diner heard that the bar does not take inbound tourists. ¥1,000 table charge; open to 1:00, irregular closing days posted monthly.

chef_bio.background: Opened 22 November 2006 (Tabelog). The name means "treasure" in Spanish (official site). A July 2026 reviewer writes that the owner holds sommelier, sake diploma and cheese professional qualifications and is known for fruit cocktails; an August 2026 diner noticed the bar's care with fresh fruit (a fruit and vegetable wash, a food-preservation spray behind the counter). Diners in 2026 describe the master as kind, modest and good at suggesting drinks. Selected for Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Colour in everyday life; one glass of magic to take you out of it" — a place to drink casually, alone or with someone dear (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fresh-fruit cocktails; home-made cakes.

anecdotes.text: "I heard that they do not accept inbound tourists, which is quite rare in the Gion area where many tourists gather." — August 2026, a coffee cocktail with dessert.
"The combination of sweets and vintage whiskey is simply unbeatable." — October 2026.
"My companion had a watermelon cocktail, which was presented in a snow style." — August 2026, with cinnamon cake.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (eltesoro.jp): El tesoro (エル・テソロ)、京都祇園の BAR、エル・テソロはスペイン語で「宝物」、日常に彩りを、一杯の魔法で非日常へ、16:00〜翌1:00 (最終入店0:00、ラストオーダー0:30)、予約可能時間16:00〜18:00 (18:00以降は来店の30分前まで)、喫煙目的店、席に限りがあるので来店前に電話を、不定休 (11月の店休日は1、4、11、18、25日)、オリジナルのカクテルも含めて希望を伝えて、東山区大和大路通三条下ル三丁目弁財天町19番地 大和ビル一階 E号室、祇園四条駅から徒歩4分、三条駅から徒歩5分。食べログ: バー 百名店 2022、チャージ1,000円、12席 (カウンター8、テーブル4)、カード・QR可、2006年11月22日オープン。口コミ(2026年7月〜10月): 季節のフルーツのカクテル、手作りのケーキ、ウイスキー、マスターが親切、インバウンドの客は受けていないと聞いたという人も。

cultural_comfort.note: Order by telling the bartender what you like; an August 2026 diner heard the bar does not take inbound tourists, so call ahead.

places.name: 山元麺蔵 (Yamamoto Menzou)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat udon is the whole menu, and the signature toppings are tempura (burdock, chicken, vegetables).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the broth is a natural dashi made with bonito (official site), and most bowls carry beef, pork, chicken or egg.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Fri 10:00–16:00 (last order); Wed 10:00–15:30 (last order); Sat, Sun and holidays 10:00–17:00 (last order); closed Thursday and irregularly, posted monthly on Instagram; closes early when the noodles run out (official site; Tabelog lists 11:00 opening and the 4th Wednesday closed). Reservations: by phone on the day from 9:00 (to 11:00) for the 11:00–13:45 slots; online through TableCheck from midnight three days ahead for 9:45–10:45 and 14:00–16:30 (to 17:00 at weekends), with a credit card for the cancellation policy (official site). At your time you queue outside, order, and are seated as seats free (official site); expect 20–30 minutes (Tabelog). Cash only in the shop (official site). 18 seats: 10 at the counter, two tables for 4 (official site). Children welcome, with kids' bowls and forks (Tabelog). Three parking spaces (Tabelog). Takeout from a separate counter (official site; October 2026). Prices rose on 9 October 2026 (shop blog). Opened 27 August 2006 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Okazaki, near the zoo — 2 min from the Okazaki-koen Dobutsuen-mae bus stop, 11 min from Higashiyama Stn exit 1
places.cuisine: Freshly made, freshly boiled udon with a natural bonito dashi (official site) · hot udon: the spicy "Red Menzou Special" with burdock tempura, fried mochi and egg; beef and shaved burdock; pork; Kyoto curry udon; chicken tenderloin tempura; burdock tempura; vegetable tempura; spicy meat-miso; kitsune, ankake, tamago-toji and more · "aromatic oil" versions with garlic, ginger and leek oil · tsukemen with a hot dipping broth (beef and burdock, beef offal, curry, pork); cold zaru udon · small tempura rice bowls with egg yolk; almond tofu; bottled beer (official menu) · toriten miso udon ¥1,700 (October 2026); diners spend ¥1,000–2,999 · the signature is the crisp burdock tempura, and the noodles are so long that scissors come with them; a mini almond tofu often comes free (October 2026)
places.notes: [Udon · Okazaki, the queue-famous udon near the zoo] A small udon house in Okazaki, on land where the founder's grandmother ran an udon shop some fifty years earlier. The noodles are freshly cut and boiled, long, glossy and seriously chewy, in a dashi taken from bonito; the burdock tempura is the order everyone mentions, with chicken-tenderloin tempura close behind, and there is a spicy curry udon and cold tsukemen. Once known for long lines, it now runs on reservations: phone on the day from 9:00 or book online three days ahead, then queue briefly at your slot. Diners in 2026 single out the warm, attentive service from the owner and staff. Cash only; closed Thursdays.

roles: Run by 株式会社山元麺蔵; the person responsible named on the company page is 山元克之 (official site); reviewers mention "the owner" and "the manager" greeting tables (October–November 2026)
chef_bio.background: The founder's message on the official site (first person, unsigned) says the idea came when the company club team the founder belonged to stopped its activities; the founder's grandmother had run an udon shop on this land about fifty years earlier and raised seven children from it; the shop aims at freshly made udon, natural bonito dashi, good rice, fresh ingredients and smiles. The company page names 山元克之 as the person responsible (no romaji given). Opened 27 August 2006 (Tabelog). The shop blog (8 October 2026) announced a price rise from 9 October, citing oil, burdock, radish, chicken, bonito, packaging and wages. Tabelog Udon "Tabelog 100" 2017–2019 and Udon WEST 2020, 2022, 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: Freshly made udon, natural bonito dashi, warm rice, fresh ingredients, and smiles, greetings and thanks in the room — the things that make a meal like home (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Burdock tempura udon; chicken-tenderloin tempura; Kyoto curry udon.

anecdotes.text: "While waiting in line, they kindly offered me an umbrella to shield me from the heat and served me tea." — November 2026, a second visit.
"The udon noodles were incredibly long, and they provided a cutter for them." — October 2026, cold beef-and-burdock tsukemen.
"The clientele was mostly foreign tourists, particularly from Korea." — October 2026, curry udon.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (yamamotomenzou.com): 山元麺蔵、月・火・金 10:00〜16:00 (L.O.)、水 10:00〜15:30 (L.O.)、土・日・祝 10:00〜17:00 (L.O.)、木曜定休と不定休 (インスタグラムで毎月告知)、麺がなくなり次第終了、電話予約は当日朝9:00〜11:00 (11時〜13時45分の枠)、オンラインは3日前の午前0時から (午前9時45分〜10時45分、午後14時〜16時30分、土日祝17時)、予約時にクレジットカード必須、店でのお会計は現金のみ、予約の時間に店の前に並んで注文、席が空き次第案内、カウンター10席と4人掛けテーブル2卓、岡崎南御所町34、運営は株式会社山元麺蔵 (責任者 山元克之)、お品書き: 赤い麺蔵スペシャル、牛と土ゴボウのおうどん、京カレーうどん、鶏ささみ天うどん、土ゴボウ天うどん、香味油のうどん、つけ麺、ざるうどん、杏仁豆腐など、「想い」: ばあちゃんがうどん屋を営んでいた土地、打ちたて茹でたてのうどん、鰹でしっかりとった天然だし。店のブログ (2026年10月8日): 10月9日から価格改定。食べログ: うどん 百名店 2017〜2019、うどん WEST 百名店 2020・2022・2024、子ども可、駐車場3台、2006年8月27日オープン。口コミ(2026年10月〜11月): ゴボウ天、鶏ささみ天、長い麺にハサミ、杏仁豆腐のサービス、温かい接客、海外の客も多い。

cultural_comfort.note: The official menu has English, Korean and Chinese versions; many overseas diners (October 2026); reservations by phone or TableCheck.

places.name: 啐啄 つか本 (Sottaku Tsukamoto)

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a kaiseki course built on dashi, with fish, crab, duck and hamo (2025–2026 reviews).

places.neighborhood: Gion, on Nishi-hanamikoji street — about 5–7 min from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cuisine: An omakase kaiseki of simple, ingredient-first Japanese dishes with notably well-balanced sauces and dressings (2025–2026 reviews) · about ¥35,000–37,000 with sake (August and December 2025); diners report ¥30,000–49,999 (Tabelog) · summer 2025: corn with tomato jelly, simmered Awaji octopus, fig and walnut with sesame, charcoal-grilled hamo with salted wasabi and plum, grilled anago sushi, grilled ayu, grilled abalone, clay-pot rice with Manganji peppers · winter 2025: seiko crab, soft roe, duck, crab rice porridge · October 2026: fig and chestnut, pressed mackerel sushi, sea bream sashimi with chrysanthemum and dashi, a soup of Matsutake and hamo · Japanese sake
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, one of Kyoto's hardest seats] Eight seats at an L-shaped counter on Nishi-hanamikoji, under a framed “Sottaku Dōji”. Chef Tsukamoto cooks quiet, exact Japanese food — figs with sesame, hamo grilled over charcoal, pressed mackerel sushi, a Matsutake and hamo soup — that diners praise for its sauces and dressings rather than show. No photos, no menu talk, cash only. The shop moved here from Pontocho in 2008; one 2025 reviewer lists two Michelin stars from 2011 to 2016. Tabelog Gold 2024–2026. It is not taking new reservations, so the only way in is with a regular.

places.cuisine: An omakase that blends Japanese and Italian cooking around luxury ingredients — sea urchin, abalone, truffle, caviar, beef fillet — and the seasons (Tabelog) · from ¥46,000 including tax, plus 10% service (Tabelog); course ¥42,000 (September 2026); diners report ¥50,000–79,999 with drinks · October 2026: a crème-brûlée of black fig and foie gras terrine with buckwheat (with Alba white truffle on one night), sea urchin with dried-scallop jelly and cauliflower, kombu-pickled turnip with Spanish mackerel or sweet sea bream and caviar, chilled capellini with sweet shrimp and fruit tomato and bottarga grated as freely as you like (the signature), Ezo abalone steak with Matsutake risotto, charcoal-grilled beef fillet, a crab carbonara made without dairy, chestnut shaved ice · wine pairings by a sommelier
places.notes: [Italian · Gion, a referral-only Japanese-Italian counter] A Gion townhouse redone for its 15th year in April 2026 — grey walls, a curved copper ceiling, an L-shaped counter of ten — where chef Yamaguchi, a soba-kaiseki cook turned Italian chef, serves an omakase heavy with luxury: fig and foie gras brûlée, sea urchin, Ezo abalone on Matsutake risotto, beef fillet, and a signature chilled capellini with sweet shrimp under as much bottarga as you can face. Diners in 2026 describe a cheerful chef, jokes with regulars and a brisk pace (one course came in about 90 minutes). First visits need a referral. Tabelog Gold 2020 and Silver every other year since 2019. From ¥46,000 plus service; closed Sundays, Mondays and holidays.

Reviewers in 2026 describe the chef as cheerful and funny. Tabelog Award Gold 2020, Silver 2019 and 2021–2026; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: A "complete referral" style to keep trust with guests; serve the ingredients guests want to eat at that moment (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Chilled capellini with sweet shrimp and bottarga; abalone with Matsutake risotto.

"The pace of service is quite fast, with all dishes served within about 90 minutes." — October 2026, first visit with a regular.
"Chef Yamaguchi brings a lively spirit to the dining experience, often injecting humor into his service." — October 2026.

places.cuisine: A monthly Chinese omakase of 8–9 dishes cooked at full flame in an open kitchen, with dim sum made fresh, plus extra orders such as fried rice or mapo tofu (Tabelog) · omakase ¥25,000 (September 2026); a pairing of five drinks ¥8,900 (September 2026); diners report ¥20,000–39,999 · signature: a swan-shaped pastry of potato dough around daikon, honey-cooked apple and blue cheese (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · 2026: kombu-cured abalone or sea bream with top-grade jellyfish and herb-lemon sauce, char siu with pickled tomato and myoga, freshly steamed shrimp shumai and xiao long bao, Peking duck (breast skin, then back), shark fin, Kagoshima beef fillet, octopus with Sichuan-pepper noodles, a wonton soup with Omi beef offal, Peking duck ramen · a "super high heat" fried rice as an extra · takeaway XO sauce (September 2026)
places.notes: [Chinese · Kiyamachi-Nijo, six seats in front of the wok] A Kyoto townhouse beside the Kiyamachi-Nijo police box where six diners watch owner-chef Kaname Miyatani (宮谷要) cook at fierce flame and over clouds of steam, the energy of a Hong Kong kitchen that won the chef over as a teenager. The course changes monthly: a swan of potato pastry around daikon, apple and blue cheese, dim sum steamed to order, Peking duck in two courses, shark fin, and fried rice from the hottest burner in Japan, as one reviewer put it, if you add it. Diners find it light and never greasy. Seats are booked to about 2030; newcomers can try for leftover seats by Instagram DM on the 1st of each month. Tabelog Silver 2026.

roles: Owner-chef (official site: "Guuオーナーシェフ　宮谷　要")

The chef's big, warm personality keeps the room loud with laughter, and visiting chefs come to eat. Mostly by referral; Tabelog opens a few new slots a year. Tabelog Silver 2026. Expect ¥40,000–59,999.

places.cuisine: A kaiseki course rooted in tea kaiseki, served on museum-grade tableware by Rosanjin and Eiraku, with Taisho-era glass and contemporary pieces (Tabelog) · about ¥57,000 with drinks (May 2026); diners report ¥50,000–79,999 · May 2026: eel Yawata-maki (a May-only dish), thin soybean kuzu tofu with abalone, a soup of fried carp with yomogi noodles, lightly seared aburame sashimi, seared bonito with wild garlic and myoga, sea bream chumaki sushi with edamame, grilled young ayu · June 2026: a clear soup of hamo and ume · October 2026: Matsutake · a welcome cup of ume kombu tea (May 2026) · sake and wine
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Anekoji, tea-kaiseki cooking on Rosanjin ware] A Sukiya-style house from the early Showa era, once a tea-utensil shop, left almost as it was: a broad entrance, a small inner garden, a counter of five or six and a four-and-a-half-mat room down the corridor. Chef Shinichi Iida, who trained in Kanazawa and Kyoto, has haunted antique shops since apprentice days, and the course comes on pieces by Rosanjin and Eiraku alongside Taisho glass. The cooking keeps to the shape of tea kaiseki — eel Yawata-maki in May, a hamo and ume soup in June, Matsutake in autumn — and reviewers call the clear soups the measure of the place. No photos of the food, cash only, and nearly every seat goes to regulars and their guests. Tabelog Gold every year from 2019 to 2026.

roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: "The chef, Shinichi Iida"; 2026 reviews: "the owner")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: trained in Kanazawa and Kyoto; built the cooking on tea kaiseki; since training days has visited antique shops whenever possible, valuing the "harmony between food and tableware"; uses works by Rosanjin and Eiraku, Taisho-era glass and contemporary pieces; fell in love with an early-Showa Sukiya-style house that was a tea-utensil shop and left it nearly untouched apart from the counter and kitchen. A May 2026 reviewer gives 2010 as the opening year and says the chef opened it. Reviewers in 2026 describe the owner as warm and engaging, explaining dishes in the private room. Tabelog Award Gold 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Harmony between food and vessel; a chance to touch the depth of Japanese culture through a meal (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Tea-kaiseki courses on Rosanjin and Eiraku ware; clear soups.

anecdotes.text: "This is the only month when I can enjoy the eel Yawata-maki from the May menu!" — May 2026, a ninth visit.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gosho-nishi, a former Wakuden head chef's dashi theatre] Natural wood, a counter of nine and private rooms near the west side of the Imperial Palace, in the building where the chef struck good well water while opening in 2017. places.cuisine: A Kyoto kaiseki of the day's best ingredients, bought at markets and fishing ports by the chef, served to everyone at once with theatre at the counter (Tabelog; official site) · lunch ¥22,000, dinner ¥44,000 including tax and service, varying with the market (official site) · July 2026 lunch: watermelon juice, grilled Mikawa eel, box sushi for the Gion Matsuri, hamo in mixed rice, a corn tempura dessert · September 2026: abalone and liver rice porridge, octopus with home-made karasumi in a chestnut burr, sweet sea bream soup, flounder sashimi cut by the chef, an extra-large cutlassfish grilled over charcoal, sesame tofu made with warabi starch; at dinner somen with crab and caviar, sushi handed over by the chef, shark-fin soup and an all-you-can-eat marinated tuna rice bowl · May 2026: Awaji hamo with egg yolk and water eggplant, young Lake Biwa ayu with watermelon sauce, nodoguro with wakame jelly · Japanese sake and wine
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Yasaka-dori, a showman's Kyoto kaiseki] Up steps on Yasaka-dori south of Kennin-ji, past guardian figures at the door, thirteen guests at a counter with a big charcoal grill in the middle watch a crew of apprentices and chef Hiroshi Sasaki work, and everyone starts together. The chef buys at markets and fishing ports and serves the day's best with wit and some theatre: abalone porridge, a cutlassfish so big it is called a dragon, sushi handed across the counter, a dessert of corn tempura. Born in Nara in 1961 into a family of cooks, the chef ran Fujita in Pontocho at 27 and opened Gion Sasaki in 1998, moving here in 2006; 2026 reviewers note seven straight years of three Michelin stars. One July 2026 diner found the apprentices did most of the cooking that day. Book by phone at the start of each month for two months ahead. Lunch ¥22,000, dinner ¥44,000 all in.

The group also runs Gion Rakumi, Sushi Rakumi and Shoku Bar Rakumi (official site). Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2021, 2023, 2024, 2026, Silver 2022, 2025; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2025.

places.cuisine: Traditional Kyoto kaiseki with no menu and no explanations, so that diners wonder what each dish is; the price of the course decides the fish for sashimi and the grill rather than the number of dishes (2026 reviews) · lunch ¥15,730 including tax, plus 10% service (October 2026); diners report about ¥6,000–19,999 at lunch and ¥30,000–39,999 at dinner · August 2026: a persimmon or quince aperitif, assorted starters with ginger, a shrimp dumpling soup, white miso in summer, winter melon, a swordfish soup tied with mitsuba, grilled sea bream, young ayu tempura, kuzu noodles, a cold rice porridge, ume as a dessert, sweet beans with matcha · October 2026: salt-grilled sea bream collar, sashimi of sea bream, squid and bonito with salt vinegar · an original sake served ice-cold in a metal vessel (August 2026)
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Demachiyanagi, a quiet old-school Kyoto counter] A wooden townhouse in a lane across from the Kitamura Art Museum, with a seven-seat counter downstairs where a still, focused chef cooks in full view and three tatami rooms upstairs. Chef Wataru Hayashi, more than fifty years in the trade, has run the place for over thirty: plain, deeply seasoned Kyoto cooking without show, from a shrimp dumpling soup to a salt-grilled sea bream collar and a cold rice porridge. There is no menu and no explanation — the house style is to let you guess. The counter is hushed (one diner found it tense) and allows no photos; the upstairs rooms are more relaxed. Lunch from about ¥15,700 is the gentle way in. Tabelog Silver or Bronze every year since 2019. Closed Wednesdays; JCB and AMEX only.

places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a Chinese course with sauces such as fermented black bean and liver sauce, fried rice and cold noodles (2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Chinese course of shark fin, abalone, chicken, pork and beef in superior broth (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.cuisine: Modern Kyoto-style Chinese: Chinese technique with Japanese finesse, served kappo-style in a machiya with a small garden (Tabelog) · signature: shark fin simmered, then grilled, in a full-bodied superior broth (Tabelog) · diners report ¥30,000–39,999 · October 2026: abalone fried with liver sauce, chicken wings stuffed with bird's nest with char siu and Gorgonzola, saury marinated in Shaoxing wine, braised shark fin, roast beef, free-range chicken with Matsutake, saury fried rice, almond shaved ice with muscat and pear; stir-fried beef with fermented black beans; fried rice with grated daikon; Tianjin rice; shirasu fried rice and cold noodles · September 2026: abalone risotto, Hyogo sweet shrimp with scallion oil, char siu · Shaoxing wine in small jars (also with soda), wine and champagne
places.notes: [Chinese · Higashiyama, Chinese cooking with a kappo soul] At the end of a quiet lane near Yasaka Shrine, a machiya with a white noren and a small garden looks like a kappo, and the ten-seat counter works like one. Chef Kentaro Nishibuchi, from Joyo in Kyoto Prefecture, learned Chinese cooking for six years at Kakan in the Kyoto Brighton Hotel, then five years of Japanese cooking at Gion Sasaki, and opened here in 2013. The result is gentle, layered Chinese food: shark fin braised and then grilled in superior broth, chicken wings stuffed with bird's nest, fried rice lightened with grated daikon. Diners in 2026 praise the chef's warm smile and call it very hard to book. Tabelog Silver every year since 2019. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Kentaro Nishibuchi (Tabelog; no kanji in a source)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in Joyo, Kyoto Prefecture; six years learning the basics of Chinese cooking at Kakan, the Chinese restaurant of the Kyoto Brighton Hotel; then five years at the kappo Gion Sasaki (kyoto_gion_sasaki in this data) to learn Japanese cooking; opened Nishibuchi Hanten near Yasaka Shrine in 2013. Tabelog praises the chef's spirit of exploration and warm smile. In September 2026 the restaurant cooked a two-day special course in Tokyo, including an Amex cardholder event and a collaboration with Yoshidashioto (September 2026 reviews); one September 2026 diner heard an Italian restaurant would open nearby. Tabelog Award Silver 2019–2026; Chinese WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2024, 2026.
chef_bio.specialty: Shark fin in superior broth; bird's-nest-stuffed chicken wings; daikon fried rice.

anecdotes.text: "Nishibuchi Hanten's fried rice includes grated daikon radish, but I wonder if other places offer this as well." — October 2026, a third visit.
"It's a popular restaurant that's hard to get a reservation at, so I reached out to various people, and this time I was fortunate enough to be offered a seat." — September 2026.
"The signature dish, chicken wings served in a bird's nest, pairs perfectly with blue cheese and is absolutely delicious." — October 2026.

places.name: 安参 (Yassan)
places.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; beef sashimi comes with ponzu or ume paste, grilled cuts and the stew are seasoned with a long-kept sauce (miso-based, per an October 2026 diner) (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a beef restaurant — beef sashimi, grilled beef and oxtail stew (Tabelog; official site).
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–22:30; closed Sunday and holidays (official site; Tabelog). The ground-floor counter takes no reservations — diners queue from before 18:00 or try around 20:00; the upstairs tatami rooms can be booked for groups of three or more (official site; 2026 reviews). Counter of about 22 on the ground floor, tatami rooms upstairs (Tabelog). Smoking allowed, per Tabelog. No photos of the raw meat (2026 reviews). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). The house was renovated for earthquake safety and reopened in March 2025 with the old interior kept (Tabelog). About 10 min from Gion-Shijo Stn; across the street from Gion Ichiriki-tei (official site). Mail order through OMAKASE and Ikyu (official site).
places.neighborhood: Gion, a townhouse with red lanterns on the north side of the main street, across from Gion Ichiriki-tei — about 10 min from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cuisine: Gion beef kappo with no menu: dishes come in order, light to rich, to your appetite — pickled cucumber and a cold oxtail soup with grated yam, then about four beef sashimi (tongue, heart, lean, blanched tripe with ponzu or ume), grilled cuts, and the oxtail stew (Tabelog; official site; 2026 reviews) · the oxtail stew, made since the founder's day by adding to the same sauce, with tongue, heart, cheek and sirloin, potatoes and eggs; eat the tail with your hands at the end; Kujo green onion and mustard on the side (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · grilled: tongue, liver, skirt, sirloin rolled around kaiware sprouts (2026 reviews) · oden; white rice to make a stew bowl · diners spend about ¥10,000–19,999 · gourd sake at New Year (Tabelog) · beer, barley-shochu sodas, sake
places.notes: [Beef · Gion, a family meat counter since 1948] Look for the red lanterns across from Ichiriki-tei: inside, a long, Showa-red counter under hanging gourds, packed and loud with Kyoto dialect. The founder, from 門前仲町 in Tokyo, opened in 1948 and created the oxtail stew that still simmers in a big pot behind the counter, its sauce topped up for over 77 years; the second generation turned it into meat kappo. There is no menu: the staff lead you from cold oxtail soup through beef-tongue, heart and tripe sashimi to grilled cuts and the stew, which you finish by picking up the bones. The counter cannot be booked, so queue before 18:00. Now run by fourth-generation Yoshifumi Sakakibara with family. Tabelog Bronze 2025–2026. Closed Sundays and holidays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshifumi Sakakibara (Tabelog; no kanji in a source)
roles: Fourth-generation chef (Tabelog: "took over as the fourth generation")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: born in Kyoto in 1994, the founder's first great-grandchild; drawn to cooking by watching the grandfather, the second generation, in the kitchen; trained from 19 at local Japanese restaurants and butchers, then apprenticed at Yassan under the senior cooks; took over at 26 as the fourth generation, running the restaurant with family: a sister, Tomoyo, a mother, Yuko, and a grandmother, Nobe, the head of the house. The official site says the first owner, from 門前仲町 in Tokyo, created the oxtail stew in Kyoto in 1948 and the second generation made it a meat kappo. Tabelog adds that it began in Teramachi-Rokkaku and moved to Gion around 1968. An October 2026 reviewer calls it a long-time favourite of actors. Tabelog Award Bronze 2025, 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep the order of dishes, light to rich, unchanged since the founding (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Oxtail stew; beef-tongue sashimi; blanched tripe with ume.

anecdotes.text: "The details of the sauce are a secret, but the stew becomes delicious by including various parts like tongue, heart, cheek meat, and sirloin." — the chef, on Tabelog.
"I arrived at 17:40 on a weekday and found five people waiting outside." — October 2026.
"I started with the beef tongue sashimi, followed by heart and lean cuts. No photos allowed." — September 2026, first visit after queuing.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gion-yassan.com): 祇園肉割烹 安参（やっさん）、創業昭和二三年、東京 門前仲町出の初代が京都でテールの煮込みを創り上げ、二代目が肉割烹へ押し上げ、安参独自のスタイルを受け継ぐ、和風の落ち着いた店内、カウンター席と個室、東山区祇園町北側347、祇園四条駅から徒歩10分ほど、祇園一力亭の向かい側の道を渡り2分、お座敷席のみ予約可 (3人以上)、18:00〜22:30、日曜・祝日休み、お取り寄せ (OMAKASE、一休.com)。食べログ: 肉料理・日本料理、1階カウンター22席と2階の座敷、喫煙可、カード可、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2025・2026、四代目は1994年生まれ。口コミ (2026年9〜10月、英語): 並んでカウンターへ、生肉の撮影は不可、タンの刺身、牛の胃、テールの煮込み、Kujo のねぎと辛子。

cultural_comfort.note: No menu: staff lead you through the dishes; counter by queue only; tatami rooms bookable for 3+.

places.name: 祇園 にし (Gion Nishi)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a kaiseki course seasoned with soy sauce and miso, with somen, sushi and an optional curry at the end (2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a kaiseki course built on dashi, with sea urchin, hamo, beef and foie gras (2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Dinner from 18:00 Tue–Sun; lunch from 12:00 Thu–Sun; closed Monday and irregularly (Tabelog; official site); evening times can be discussed (Tabelog). Reservations by phone (August 2026). 20 seats: a counter of 6 and tables for up to 14 (Tabelog). Children who can eat the course are welcome (Tabelog). Non-smoking, with an ashtray at the entrance (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR payments (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay); service charge 10% (Tabelog). About 8 min from Gion-Shijo Stn: from the Higashiyama-Yasui crossing go about 50 m along Higashioji-dori, on the left (Tabelog). Opened 7 July 2016 (Tabelog). GION NISHI CAFE is on the floor above (official site).
places.neighborhood: Near Yasaka Shrine, on Higashioji-dori about 50 m from the Higashiyama-Yasui crossing — about 8 min from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cuisine: Kaiseki with an Italian-trained chef's ideas — ingredients and techniques Japanese cooking does not usually use — and a showpiece hassun (official site; Tabelog) · lunch omakase ¥19,360 including tax and service (August 2026); dinner a little under ¥30,000 (August 2026) · June 2026: 長芋素麺と蓴菜に大間の雲丹, a white-miso bowl of 牡丹鱧, sashimi of aori squid, tuna, sea urchin and nodoguro, a hassun with lobster and corn mousse, 鮎の海苔巻き寿司, beef loin and Kamo eggplant with shrimp dengaku · August 2026: chawanmushi of sea urchin, abalone, shrimp, crab and caviar; a soup of ayu, Matsutake and winter melon; grilled hamo, squid and trout sashimi · curry to finish on request (July, August 2026) · wine chosen by the owner, a certified sommelier, and sake from a certified sake expert (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Kaiseki · near Yasaka Shrine, kaiseki with an Italian twist and good wine] A calm room of a six-seat counter and tables a few minutes from Yasaka Shrine, run by owner-chef Jumpei Nishi (西隼平), born in Kyoto Prefecture in 1983, who trained at Tokuwo, spent time in an Italian kitchen and ran a Gion kitchen before opening in 2016. The cooking keeps kaiseki form but borrows Italian ideas, with a hassun that is the centrepiece and luxuries like a chawanmushi of sea urchin, abalone and caviar. The chef is a certified sommelier and sake expert and pours by the glass to your taste; you can even ask for curry at the end. A Japanese review praises the okami's care. Lunch ¥19,360 all in is good value for the area. Tabelog Bronze every year since 2019. Closed Mondays.

roles: Certified wine sommelier and sake expert (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1983 in Kyoto Prefecture; trained at the Kyoto Japanese restaurant Tokuwo, then at an Italian restaurant to broaden the cooking; head chef at a Japanese restaurant in Gion before opening Gion Nishi in July 2016. The official site says the chef brings young sensibility and Italian essence to Japanese tradition and actively uses ingredients and techniques Japanese cooking does not; the shop also produces GION NISHI CAFE upstairs. A June 2026 Japanese review praises the 大将's delicate cooking and the 女将 and staff's care. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: No compromise on ingredients, drink, tableware or space; original dishes made with playfulness (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: The hassun; kaiseki with Italian touches; wine pairings.

anecdotes.text: "Even when I requested curry, they served it with a smile, without any hint of displeasure." — July 2026.
"I opted for the Omakase course priced at JPY 19,360 (including tax and service charge)." — August 2026, lunch.
"When I shared my preferences, they served me a glass from a bottle they had." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gion-nishi.com): 祇園 にし、店主・西隼平は日本料理店とイタリアンで修行、日本料理の伝統に若い感性とイタリアンのエッセンス、食材・お酒・器・空間に妥協しない、日本料理では扱わない食材や技法も取り入れる、八坂神社の近く、二階に GION NISHI CAFE、東山区月見町21-2 1階、月曜全日と不定休。食べログ (店舗会員): 火・水は夜のみ、木〜日は昼と夜、20席 (カウンター6、テーブル14)、カードと QR 可、サービス料10%、2016年7月7日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。口コミ (2026年6月、日本語): 大将の繊細で工夫に満ちた料理、女将さんやスタッフの細やかな気遣い、長芋素麺と蓴菜に大間の雲丹、牡丹鱧の白味噌仕立てのお椀、アオリイカ・マグロ・雲丹・ノドグロのお造り、オマール海老やとうもろこしのムースの八寸、鮎の海苔巻き寿司、牛ロースと賀茂茄子の海老の田楽。

cultural_comfort.note: One omakase course; book by phone; drinks chosen to your taste; QR payments including Alipay and WeChat Pay.

places.name: 真白 (MASHIRO)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; French-based cooking that uses soy sauce and miso in its sauces (Tabelog), with a rice-cracker cup for the opening sea urchin and vegetable fritters in 2026.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood-led course with beef, lamb and chicken (2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Lunch from 12:00 and dinner from 18:00, each starting together; closed irregularly (official site; Tabelog). Reservation only, online (official site); a July 2026 diner booked 63 days ahead on TableCheck. 11 seats at a counter cut from a single slab over 10 m long (Tabelog). Children from 10, on the adult course (Tabelog). Smart casual (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair access (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). 4 min from Karasuma Oike Stn exit 5, 6 min from Karasuma Stn exit 21 (official site). Opened 20 August 2023 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Near Rokkakudo, OHG京都六角ビル 2F — 4 min from Karasuma Oike Stn exit 5
places.cuisine: Genre-free cooking on a French base, with a drop of soy sauce or miso and a pinch of spice, built on produce sent direct from growers (official site; Tabelog) · the only fixed dish is the opening "Uni" (read "umi"): creamy sea urchin and a seawater jelly in a rice-cracker cup, eaten in one bite (Tabelog) · pairing ¥8,800 at lunch, ¥11,000 at dinner, from champagne, sake and white, red, rosé and orange wines (Tabelog) · diners report ¥15,000–19,999 at lunch and ¥30,000–39,999 at dinner · roasted managatsuo under Parmesan "fish bones" (Tabelog) · September 2026: Yosano-rice mushroom risotto with fresh salmon roe, caviar with Shinkansen pear and burrata, Korean mackerel, French lamb with peanut sprouts · October 2026: a rice-porridge soup, scallops with porcini, local chicken, a near-two-metre cutlassfish, Tajima beef top sirloin · August 2026: Hida beef · message plates for celebrations (Tabelog; July–August 2026)
places.notes: [French · Karasuma-Rokkaku, a genre-free chef's counter] A second-floor room near Rokkakudo with a single-slab counter over ten metres long, hexagonal tiles that nod to the temple, and an open kitchen run like a show. The chef trained at the Rihga Royal Hotel in Osaka, became the youngest chef in its history at 33 at Restaurant Chambord in 小倉, went to the 2015 Bocuse d'Or Japan final, and won Michelin stars at Cosimo Plus in Ashiya and Gion Roshoku before opening MASHIRO in 2023. Every meal opens with "Uni", sea urchin and seawater jelly in a rice-cracker cup; after that the course follows the market, with French sauces sharpened by soy or miso. Pairings come from sommelier-manager Masahiro Kobayashi, a partner of over 20 years. Tabelog Bronze 2026. Book online well ahead.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hiroyuki Koshimo (Tabelog's chef heading; the same listing also writes "Kosimo", "Koshiro" and "Kosumo"; no kanji in a source read)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: trained at the Rihga Royal Hotel in Osaka and at 33 became the youngest chef in the hotel's history, at the 小倉 grand maison Restaurant Chambord; then chef at DOUZE GOUT 12+ in Kyoto; a Japan finalist for the Bocuse d'Or 2015; opened コシモ・プリュス in Ashiya in May 2012 (one Michelin star, Kyoto-Osaka 2014) and 祇園 呂色 in November 2017 (one star, 2018); opened MASHIRO in Karasuma-Rokkaku in August 2023. The name means "pure white": reset your mind and enjoy the food with all six senses. The sommelier and manager, Masahiro Kobayashi, has worked with the chef for over 20 years (Tabelog). The site lists tie-in plans with the 南座 theatre (2026). Tabelog Award Bronze 2026; Innovative/Creative "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Tradition matters, but as Japanese French cuisine we must change something" (Tabelog); "Make your heart pure white" (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: The opening "Uni"; market-led courses; pairings.

anecdotes.text: "The chef kindly included a birthday message and a note related to my favorite artist on the final dessert plate." — July 2026, lunch.
"Every month, I look forward to dining at MASHIRO!" — September 2026, a fourteenth visit.
"The ribbonfish, which looks massive, is said to be nearly 2 meters long, and its fat is exquisite." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (mashiro-kyoto.com): 真白 MASHIRO ジャンルレス料理、真白な空気で深呼吸し1日が始まる、毎朝生産者から届く最高の食材、漬・焼・煮・蒸・揚・発酵・熟成、シェフは大阪「リーガロイヤルホテル」で修業、同ホテル史上最年少の33歳で小倉「レストラン シャンボール」のシェフ、京都「DOUZE GOUT 12＋」のシェフ、ボキューズ・ドール2015日本代表ファイナリスト、2012年5月 芦屋に「コシモ・プリュス」(ミシュラン京都・大阪2014で一つ星)、2017年11月「祇園 呂色」(2018で一つ星)、2023年8月 烏丸・六角に「真白」、「心を真っ白に」、堂之前町234 OHG京都六角ビル2階、ランチ12:00〜・ディナー18:00〜 一斉スタート、不定休、南座とのタイアッププラン。食べログ (店舗会員): カウンター11席、10歳以上、スマートカジュアル、サービス料10%、ペアリング 昼8,800円・夜11,000円、2023年8月20日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2026。口コミ (2026年7〜10月、英語): 名物の雲丹、メッセージプレート、季節の魚、ペアリング。

cultural_comfort.note: Book online; the official site has an English page; one course with a shared start.

places.name: 室町和久傳 (Muromachi Wakuden)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a kaiseki course seasoned with soy sauce and miso, with fried dishes and sushi among the closing rices (2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Ask: the official site lists a shojin (Buddhist vegetarian) course at ¥25,000, bookable up to three days ahead, and Tabelog marks vegetarian options; whether it uses any animal-based dashi or egg is not stated. The regular courses use fish, eel, turtle and beef.
places.hours_raw: Lunch Mon, Fri, Sat, Sun 12:00–15:00 (last seating 13:00); dinner 18:00–21:00 (Tabelog: last seating 19:00, to 22:00); closed Wednesday; also closed 5 November and 25–30 December 2026 (official site; Tabelog). Reservation requested, online or by phone (official site). Cancellation the day before or on the day: 80% (official site). 50 seats: a counter of 15 and four private rooms for 4–20 (Tabelog). Counter from junior-high age; children of any age in the private rooms, with a kids' menu and strollers welcome (Tabelog). English menu (Tabelog). Wheelchair accessible; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards accepted; prices include tax and service (official site). 5 min east of Karasuma Oike Stn exit 3-1 (official site).
places.neighborhood: Sakaimachi-dori below Oike, in a renovated machiya with a garden — 5 min from Karasuma Oike Stn
places.cuisine: Kyoto ryotei cooking at a counter that surrounds the chefs, from a house that began as an inn in Tango in 1870 (Tabelog) · lunch ¥13,000 / ¥25,000 / ¥35,000; dinner ¥25,000 / ¥35,000; sake pairing courses lunch ¥23,000, dinner ¥37,000 or ¥50,000; crab course about ¥70,000 (November–March); shojin course ¥25,000 (book three days ahead); all including tax and service (official site) · autumn 2026: a chrysanthemum dish of crab, sea urchin and caviar in jelly for the Choyo festival; fried ayu with chestnuts; seared bonito with dill; a Matsutake dobin-mushi with eel; narai-yaki — eel wrapped around Matsutake, a house dish of some fifty years; turtle and mushroom hot pot; Kyoto beef fillet; a choice of three closing rices (turtle zosui, saba sushi, beef sukiyaki on rice), with leftovers made into onigiri to take home; Uji matcha (September–October 2026) · sake pairings
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Sakaimachi-Oike, a ryotei house's counter] The town branch of Wakuden, a Kyoto ryotei family that began as an inn in Tango in 1870: a renovated machiya with a garden, a counter of fifteen around a crew of young cooks, and private rooms for families. Courses follow the season — in autumn a chrysanthemum dish for the Choyo festival, Matsutake in a teapot soup, and narai-yaki, eel wrapped around Matsutake, a house dish for half a century — and end with a choice of clay-pot rices, the rest wrapped as onigiri for later. A shojin course is available if you book three days ahead. About half the guests one September 2026 night were from overseas, with explanations in English. Some 2026 diners found it salty or routine. Lunch from ¥13,000 all in; closed Wednesdays.

roles: Run by Wakuden Inc. (official site's copyright: "wakuden Inc.")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: the Wakuden house was established in 1870 as a ryokan in Tango; the Muromachi restaurant is a Kyoto townhouse built by Nakamura Sotoku Construction (as Tabelog's English gives it), with a counter designed so every seat watches the chefs. The official site lists the group's other ryotei (Kodaiji Wakuden, Kyoto Wakuden), soba and other restaurants, and gift shops in Kyoto, Tokyo and Nagoya. An October 2026 reviewer calls the house a training ground for chefs such as those of Tokuwo and Kiyama (kyoto_kiyama_gosho in this data). Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2022, 2025, 2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Serve the true flavours of each season, nurtured by nature, with sincerity (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Narai-yaki of eel and Matsutake; clay-pot rice; seasonal kaiseki at the counter.

anecdotes.text: "Almost half of the guests were from overseas, and the staff provided explanations in English." — September 2026.
"Their signature rice was wonderfully sticky, and they even made the leftovers into onigiri for me to take home." — September 2026.
"There were many dishes that were overly salty." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (wakuden.jp): 室町和久傳、京都市中京区堺町通り御池下ル東側、昼12時〜15時 (月・金・土・日のみ)、13,000円・25,000円・35,000円、夜18時〜21時 25,000円・35,000円、日本酒ペアリングコース (昼23,000円、夜37,000円・50,000円)、蟹のコース70,000円前後 (11月〜3月)、精進25,000円 (3日前までの予約)、水曜定休、11月5日と12月25日〜30日は休み、料金は税・サービス料込み、前日・当日キャンセルは80%、クレジットカード可、烏丸御池駅3-1出口から東へ徒歩5分。和久傳のほかの店: 高台寺和久傳、京都和久傳、蕎麦と料理の店、おもたせの店。食べログ (店舗会員): 1870年に Tango の旅館として創業、町家、カウンター15席と個室4室、カウンターは中学生以上、子どもは個室で、英語メニュー、ベジタリアンメニューあり、The Tabelog Award Bronze、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。口コミ (2026年9〜10月、英語): Matsutake の dobin-mushi、鰻で Matsutake を巻いた narai 焼き、締めのご飯が3種類、残りはおにぎりに、海外の客が多く英語で説明、塩気が強いという声も。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu (Tabelog) and English explanations for overseas guests (September 2026); book online.

places.name: 京 静華 (Kyo Seika)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking by phone. No gluten information; the course includes spring rolls, steamed buns, noodles and Sichuan-style sauces (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Chinese course of shark fin, abalone, sea cucumber, crab, char siu and wagyu (2025–2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Dinner only, everyone starting at 18:00; closed Monday and Tuesday and irregularly — check the calendar on the official site (official site; Tabelog). The restaurant closed from 1 May 2026 for maintenance and training and reopened in September 2026 (official site). Bookings by phone only, up to the end of the month two months ahead, 11:00–16:00 on business days; not by Instagram or Facebook messages (official site). Cancellation: 100% on the day, 50% the day before; no children below junior-high age except for whole-room bookings (official site). 16 seats: a round table for 10 and two tables for 3 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards accepted; service charge 10% (Tabelog). The site warns of fake websites using its name. About 5 min from Higashiyama Stn (Tabelog). Opened 20 April 2008 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Okazaki, second floor near Heian Shrine and the Biwako Sosui canal — about 5 min from Higashiyama Stn (Tozai Line)
places.cuisine: Delicate Chinese cooking that recreates methods from classical Chinese texts, with Kyoto morning-market vegetables (Tabelog) · seasonal course ¥25,000 (¥27,500 including tax), plus 10% service; special menus for whole-room bookings of up to 6 (official site; Tabelog) · the spring roll with a spicy sorbet opens most meals, with seasonal fillings: young ayu, firefly squid and caciocavallo (April 2026); scallop, truffle and caciocavallo (December 2025); butterbur and firefly squid (March 2026) · October 2025: a soup of shark fin, abalone, Matsutake and sea cucumber; char siu with figs; wagyu; crab sticky rice, meat buns and mushroom noodles from the steamer · December 2025: soft roe with a Sichuan sauce; a lotus-root cake · October 2026: Doman crab, black abalone, Densuke eel; congee · wine pairings with Burgundy and champagne; Shaoxing wine
places.notes: [Chinese · Okazaki, a master's quiet Chinese table near Heian Shrine] A second-floor room by the Biwako Sosui canal, one round table and two small ones, everyone starting at 18:00. Owner-chef Shizuo Miyamoto ran Seika in Hamamatsu for 25 years from 1983, trained in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Beijing, studied again in Beijing in middle age, and opened here in 2008; dishes recreate techniques from classical Chinese texts with Kyoto vegetables. Every meal starts with a crisp spring roll and a spicy sorbet, and the course runs through shark fin and abalone soups, char siu and steamer baskets of crab rice and buns. After two apprentices left to open their own places, the restaurant closed from May 2026 and reopened in September with the chef cooking alone. ¥27,500 including tax, plus service; book by phone. Tabelog Bronze in most years since 2017.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Higashiyama, a century-old ryotei by Kodai-ji] Up the slope past Maruyama Park, beside Kodai-ji, a ryotei founded in the first year of the Taisho era by a family that kept the spring "Kikusui no I" once used for Nene's tea. Third-generation owner Yoshihiro Murata, born in 1951, trained in France and Nagoya before taking up the family craft, and has led the push to have washoku listed by UNESCO. Meals are served in ten tatami rooms over the garden, some hung with works such as Ito Jakuchu screens, with a new seasonal menu every month: Matsutake and hamo in a teapot soup, ayu shown alive before grilling, tuna with egg-yolk soy sauce. The site reports three Michelin stars in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Lunch from ¥16,500 plus 15% service is the gentle way in.

The official site lists the house's other restaurants (露庵, 赤坂菊乃井, 無碍山房) and three Michelin stars in the Kyoto-Osaka guides 2024, 2025 and 2026. A September 2026 diner was greeted by the owner. chef_bio.philosophy: Cooking with water: vegetables simmered in dashi to carry flavour, and the spirit of the tea ceremony (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Kyoto kappo of the day's best ingredients — natural ayu, turtle, gurnard, bamboo shoots, Matsutake — cooked with a light hand, as a course or à la carte at market prices (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews) · course ¥22,000 (July 2026); à la carte at market price, e.g. first-of-season torigai ¥8,500 (July 2026); diners report ¥15,000–39,999 with drinks · three starters to begin, e.g. anago sushi, hamo tempura with shiso and ume, yuba (October 2025) · spring 2026: Tsukahara bamboo shoots as sashimi and grilled; Omi beef with flower pepper; simmered sea bream; shrimp taro with crab sauce; rice steamed in bamboo · summer 2026: hamo grilled half-done on a shichirin at the counter; sea urchin; sea-bream crackers · September 2026: marinated hamo with corn and muscat; Wakasa gurnard sashimi and grilled head; turtle stew and turtle hot pot; grilled meat with rice and red miso soup · sake such as Michizakari and Kuro-ryu
places.notes: [Kappo · Gion, a classic counter where you can order à la carte] An old-style house in a Gion lane: a wood counter of nine full of regulars and a lively voice behind it, sunken seats, and tatami rooms upstairs. Chef Hirokazu Sakagawa trained at Kappo Nakagawa in north Gion before opening here in the Heisei era. The draw is choice: take the course or order à la carte from the day's ingredients — bamboo shoots from Tsukahara in spring, hamo grilled on a shichirin in summer, Wakasa gurnard and turtle in autumn — and the kitchen cooks them as you like. Regulars order at their own pace; first-timers find the chef quietly welcoming. Market prices can climb (one September 2026 evening came to ¥39,000 with drinks). Tabelog Bronze every year since 2019. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Higashiyama, a warm chef's sukiya house below Yasaka Shrine] Down a stone-paved lane between Yasaka Shrine and Kodaiji, a sukiya-style house of bamboo and hinoki with a single-slab counter 7.5 metres long and a small garden visible from every room. Owner-chef Masayoshi Nishikawa, born in Kyoto in 1975 to a family of Yuzen dyers, trained at Gion Sasaki, ran the kitchen at Warabi no Sato, and opened here in 2009; a Michelin listing followed within a year, and 2026 reviewers count two stars for fifteen years running. The menu changes daily: dashi from Yasaka Shrine's soft spring water, Ohara vegetables, a pressed mackerel sushi diners rave about, and touches like caviar on grilled eggplant. Reviewers love the chef's jokes and send-offs; in September 2026 the chef was running the kitchen almost alone, with an apprentice joining in October.

chef_bio.chef_name: Masayoshi Nishikawa (Tabelog; no kanji in a source)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1975 in Kyoto Prefecture; a grandfather who was a Yuzen dyer, and a childhood among Kyoto's beautiful and delicious things, led to cooking after high school; trained at Gion Sasaki (kyoto_gion_sasaki in this data), was head chef at Warabi no Sato, and opened Gion Nishikawa (the section says 2008; the listing's opening date is 22 January 2009); motto "a wide entrance and a high exit". Tabelog adds a Michelin Guide 2010 listing just over a year after opening. A September 2026 reviewer counts two Michelin stars for 15 consecutive years, says the chef had no apprentices then and ran the kitchen almost alone, with a new apprentice joining in October; another cites the motto "Shinmi wa tada kore tan" (true flavour is simply this). Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "A wide entrance and a high exit": welcoming and friendly, with cooking of the highest standard (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Pressed mackerel sushi; Kyoto kaiseki with Yasaka Shrine water.

anecdotes.text: "I learned that he currently has no apprentices and runs the kitchen almost entirely by himself." — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Kaiseki in the spirit of Zen cooking and the tea ceremony, from a chef trained 20 years at Shofukuro (Tabelog) · diners report ¥10,000–14,999 at lunch and ¥30,000–39,999 at dinner; a ¥500 charge · sashimi with "mascarpone soy sauce" and chili vinegar (Tabelog) · February 2026: sweet shrimp and abalone with egg-yolk sauce, a crab soup, fugu dumplings, tuna sushi from Ine, Omi beef in white miso, then rice from the chef's home in Shiga with refills and toppings, and a very soft mizu-yokan · May 2026: abalone, sea urchin and sesame tofu; eggplant and rockfish soup; simmered kinmedai; young ayu; ayu sushi; marinated chutoro; fried conger eel · July 2026: Awaji sea bream, ayu grilled then lightly fried, somen in a hand-carved ice bowl, Shiga Koshihikari rice with ebi-mame, mango, a yokan from the Shofukuro tradition, matcha · Ebisu draft beer and sake
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, tea-ceremony cooking at a friendly counter] Through a noren and down a water-sprinkled stone alley off Hanamikoji, a hinoki counter of ten looks onto a small garden, with tatami rooms upstairs set with fine tableware. Chef Nobuhiko Masuda, born in Shiga in 1957, spent twenty years at the ryotei Shofukuro, opened Sangencha in Mizuguchi, Shiga, and moved to Gion; the cooking keeps the spirit of Zen cuisine and the tea meal while playing with ideas like mascarpone soy sauce for the sashimi. Courses end with rice from the chef's home town, as much as you like, and a melting mizu-yokan. Regulars come back for years for the chef's gentle humour; families are welcome, with a kids' menu. Lunch from about ¥10,000. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Nobuhiko Masuda (Tabelog; no kanji in a source)
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog chef section; 2026 reviews: "Chef Masuda", "the head chef and his apprentice")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1957 in Shiga, among lakes and mountains, influenced by a mother who cooked well; trained at a Kyoto kaiseki restaurant, then 20 years at the ryotei Shofukuro, absorbing Zen cuisine and the tea ceremony; opened Sangencha in Mizuguchi, Shiga, and moved it to Gion in 2007, from ryotei to counter. The upstairs rooms use tableware used by the British royal family and ceramics the owner chose (Tabelog). A February 2026 reviewer has visited for about 15 years. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Ichigo ichie: tradition and novelty served with a balanced pace (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Tea-kaiseki courses; Shiga rice to finish; mizu-yokan.

anecdotes.text: "I have been visiting this place occasionally for about 15 years now. The deliciousness remains unchanged." — February 2026.
"The standout dish was the somen served in a hand-carved ice bowl." — July 2026.
"As soon as you enter, the scent of incense reminds you that you are in Kyoto." — June 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 山玄茶、日本料理、東山区祇園町北側347-96、祇園四条駅から徒歩12分、月・木〜日は昼12:00〜14:30 (L.O.13:00) と夜18:00〜21:30 (L.O.19:30)、水は夜のみ、火曜と第2水曜休み、要予約、26席 (カウンター10)、個室あり、子ども可でお子様メニューあり、禁煙、カード可、チャージ500円、テイクアウト可、2008年2月8日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。口コミ (2026年2〜9月、英語): 禅と茶の湯の心、Shiga のご飯のおかわり、mizu-yokan、氷の器の素麺、大将と弟子の温かいもてなし、常連が多い。

cultural_comfort.note: One omakase course at a counter or in tatami rooms; children welcome with a kids' menu.

places.name: TAKAYAMA (タカヤマ)
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; the course of some 25 small dishes includes gnocchi fritto, a sandwich, a choux, bruschetta, risotto and sweets (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Ask: Tabelog marks vegetarian options; the standard course uses caviar, foie gras, mortadella, crab and meat (2025–2026 reviews).
places.hours_raw: Lunch from 12:00 and dinner from 18:00, each starting together and lasting about three hours; closed Monday and irregularly (official site; Tabelog). Reservation only; changes count as cancellations with a fee (Tabelog). A ¥1,000 water charge per person; service included (Tabelog). 12 seats at a curved counter around an open kitchen; whole-room hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Children only if able to stay seated through the course; no shorts or sandals; photos of the food only, and post videos muted (official site). Non-smoking; the toilets are in the building on the same floor (official site). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) (Tabelog). Parking in the GOOD NATURE STATION car park (Tabelog). 3 min from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn (Tabelog). Opened 9 December 2019 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Kawaramachi-Shijo, GOOD NATURE STATION 2F — 3 min from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn (Hankyu)
places.cuisine: "TAKAYAMA Creative Experience": a course of about 25 small creative dishes on a modern-Italian base (official site; Tabelog) · ¥30,000 including tax and service at lunch or dinner (official site); from November to 11 January only a Winter Special Course, ¥35,000 (Tabelog); plus a ¥1,000 water charge · fixtures: a welcome juice coated in white chocolate printed with a QR code that opens the menu; "Japan Caviar" from Miyazaki on squid-ink potato chips in a white box (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews) · December 2025: foie gras choux with apple jam, a Takayama sandwich with truffle ice cream, gnocchi fritto with mortadella, Seiko crab and bottarga risotto, a mountain of Ohara vegetables · wine pairings, including an Australian rosé the chef recommended (July 2026); non-alcoholic drinks · sweets you can take home (February 2026)
places.notes: [Italian · Kawaramachi-Shijo, a three-hour creative show of 25 small plates] A white room on the second floor of GOOD NATURE STATION with a curved counter of twelve around a stage-like open kitchen and no handle on the door. Owner-chef Tadashi Takayama went to Italy at 22, came home defeated by the language, went back at 27 to cook in Piedmont and Tuscany, and was sous-chef at Crescios in Campania before opening here in 2019. The course is about 25 bites built for fun as well as flavour: a juice wrapped in white chocolate with the menu as a printed QR code, Miyazaki caviar on squid-ink crisps, foie gras choux, a risotto of Seiko crab. Plan on three hours and come hungry. Many guests are from overseas, and staff are young and warm. ¥30,000 all in, plus ¥1,000 for water; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Tadashi Takayama (Tabelog; official site: "オーナーシェフ高山")
chef_bio.origin: Hiroshima Prefecture, born 1984 (Tabelog; a March 2026 review says the chef hails from Kyoto).
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section (first person): born in 1984 in Hiroshima; began training at a local Italian restaurant after junior high; from 20 worked part-time at a fish market to save for Italy; went at 22 but came back over the language barrier; returned at 27 and cooked in Piedmont and Tuscany, then was sous-chef at Crescios in Campania; opened TAKAYAMA in 2019. The official site's theme is "comfort + excitement = happiness", with conversation between guests, chefs and cooks around a full open kitchen. Tabelog Award Bronze 2025, 2026; Innovative/Creative "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Comfort + excitement = happiness" (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Japan Caviar on squid-ink crisps; the QR-code chocolate welcome drink.

anecdotes.text: "The surface of the white chocolate has a QR code that, when scanned, displays the day's menu." — September 2026.
"I arrived after a 100-minute walk along the Kamo River, just in time for lunch, which ended at 3:40 PM." — February 2026.
"I've heard foreign guests are flocking in, but more Japanese people should experience it too." — July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (takayama-kyoto.com): TAKAYAMA、テーマは「心地よさ+トキメキ＝幸せ」、フルオープンキッチンとカウンター席、季節の食材のインスピレーション溢れる創作料理、TAKAYAMA Creative Experience 昼・夜30,000円 (税サ込)、約3時間、少量多皿、オーナーシェフ高山、下京区河原町通四条下ル2丁目稲荷町318番6 GOOD NATURE STATION 2階、ランチ12時・ディナー18時の一括スタート、全席禁煙、ショートパンツやサンダル不可、子どもは最後まで着席できる場合のみ、化粧室は同フロアの館内、料理のみ撮影可。食べログ (店舗会員): イノベーティブ・創作料理・イタリアン、12席、月曜と不定休、11月〜1月11日は冬の特別コース35,000円のみ、お水代1人1,000円、サービス料込み、カード可、2019年12月9日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2025・2026、イノベーティブ・創作料理 百名店 2025。口コミ (2025年12月〜2026年9月、英語): QR コードのホワイトチョコのジュース、Japan Caviar、約25皿、海外の客が多い。

cultural_comfort.note: Many overseas guests; the official site has English and Chinese pages; the menu opens from a QR code.

places.name: LURRA°
places.gf_detail: Ask when booking, but Tabelog warns that with seasonal ingredients it may be hard to change dishes for allergies or dislikes. The courses include pasta, ravioli, tuile and doughnuts (2026 reviews).
places.vegan_detail: Ask: Tabelog marks vegetarian options, but also says allergy and preference changes may be hard; the course uses fish, horse meat and chicken (August 2026).
places.hours_raw: Tue–Sat dinner in two seatings: 17:30 at the counter (up to 10, starting together) and 18:30 at the communal table (up to 8); closed Sunday and Monday (official site; Tabelog — whose introduction says 17:30 and 20:30). Doors open 10 minutes before (Tabelog). Reservations through the official website (Tabelog). In August, a short walk-in à la carte lunch season (11–29 August in 2026; queues from about 10:30) (2026 reviews). 18 seats: 10 at the counter, 8 at one table; whole-room hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Guests 13 and over, except for private hire (Tabelog). English-speaking staff (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); service charge 10% (Tabelog). 1 min from Higashiyama Stn exit 1 (Tabelog). Opened 9 July 2019 (Tabelog).
places.neighborhood: Higashiyama, a renovated townhouse over 250 years old, a minute from Higashiyama Stn exit 1 (Tozai Line)
places.cuisine: Wood-fired "hybrid" courses that mix Nordic and Japanese fermentation with the seasons, using vegetables the chef gathers in the Ohara countryside and fish and meat direct from producers, cooked over embers in a kiln and oven (Tabelog; official site) · diners report ¥30,000–59,999 at dinner · August 2026 dinner: purple sea urchin manju, horse meat tartare, hiramasa with dried strawberries and ponzu, edamame tofu panna cotta with gazpacho jelly, ravioli, Biwa trout roasted in the fireplace with clam chowder sauce, chicken, a plate of Kyoto vegetables, seaweed risotto, melon ice cream with hojicha cookies · August lunch à la carte: kanpachi aguachile, peach pasta, zucchini pizza, a French omelette with Boursin, the LURRA° burger, mango parfait and fried ice-cream doughnuts · wine, cocktails, and a non-alcoholic pairing; drinks by Yusuke Sakaibe, a cocktail-competition champion (Tabelog)
places.notes: [Innovative · Higashiyama, Nordic-Japanese cooking over open fire] A townhouse more than 250 years old, a minute from Higashiyama station, where ten guests at the counter watch the cooks work a wood fire and oven. Chef Jacob Kear, born in California and raised in Japan, cooked at Noma in Copenhagen and Noma Tokyo and was head chef of Clooney in New Zealand; drinks come from Yusuke Sakaibe, a cocktail champion the chef met in New Zealand. The name is Basque for earth, the ring a moon. Courses mix Nordic fermentation with Japanese seasons and Ohara vegetables — sea urchin manju, Biwa trout roasted in the fireplace with clam chowder sauce, fried ice-cream doughnuts to finish. A 2026 review reports a Michelin star in the Kyoto Osaka 2026 guide. In August a casual walk-in lunch runs for a few weeks. Book online; closed Sundays and Mondays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Jacob Kear (official site; Tabelog also writes "Jacob Keer", "Jaykaub Keer" and "Jacob Kier")
chef_bio.origin: Born in California, USA, and raised in Japan (official site).
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: born in California and raised in Japan; after LA and Tokyo, trained at Noma in Copenhagen and followed it to Noma Tokyo; head chef at Clooney in New Zealand, which won three hats in the NZ Cuisine Good Food Awards. LURRA˚ means "earth" in Basque, and the ring stands for the moon; the aim is to show Japan's seasons and culture to the world. Tabelog adds that the chef and the drink specialist Yusuke Sakaibe, a cocktail-competition champion, met at a New Zealand restaurant, and that the house is a renovated townhouse over 250 years old. An August 2026 reviewer reports one star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026. Tabelog Award Bronze 2025; Innovative/Creative "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "A showcase of Japan's seasons and culture", combining innovation, tradition and nature (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Wood-fired dishes; Nordic-Japanese fermentation; fried ice-cream doughnuts.

anecdotes.text: "In front of me, they were burning firewood. Yes, real firewood." — August 2026, dinner with a non-alcoholic pairing.
"When I arrived on Friday at 10:40, there was a line, but since I was alone, I was allowed to enter first." — August 2026, à la carte lunch.
"Being able to enjoy the fried ice cream donuts during lunch was a delightful surprise." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (lurrakyoto.com): LURRA˚ はバスク語で「地球」、「°」は月の意、京都から日本の季節と文化のショーケースを世界に発信、シェフ Jacob Kear は米・カリフォルニア生まれ、LA や東京を経てデンマークの NOMA で研鑽、NOMA 東京に随行、ニュージーランドの Clooney でヘッドシェフ時代に3ハット、東山区石泉院町396、営業時間 17:30〜 (カウンター席、一斉スタート)・18:30〜 (テーブル席のみ)、定休日は日・月。食べログ (店舗会員): イノベーティブ、築250年を超える町家、Ohara の里山の野菜、窯とオーブンの熾火、季節の食材のためアレルギーや苦手な食材の変更は難しい場合あり、18席 (カウンター10、テーブル8)、13歳以上、英語を話せるスタッフ、ベジタリアンメニューあり、サービス料10%、2019年7月9日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2025、イノベーティブ・創作料理 百名店 2025。口コミ (2026年5〜8月、英語): 薪の火、8月の限定アラカルトのランチ、揚げたアイスのドーナツ、ミシュラン一つ星。

cultural_comfort.note: English-speaking staff and an English official site; book online; set course at a shared start.
